Title: The euro celebrates its 10th anniversary  The BCL at the service of the Luxembourg economy and citizens
text: THE EURO CELEBRATES ITS 10TH ANNIVERSARY  THE BCL AT THE SERVICE OF THE LUXEMBOURG ECONOMY AND CITIZENS by Mr Yves Mersch, President of the Banque centrale du Luxembourg Inter-Lycees Conference, Lycee technique du centre, 25 April 2005 Only the word spoken is authentic For my speech to you, your teachers offered me the following style exercise: project us to January 1, 2012. I will try to stick to that by presenting my working hypotheses regarding the context in which we will find ourselves on that date. I will distinguish 3 executives: 1. The European framework 2. The Eurosystem framework; and 3. The framework for decisions already taken by the Eurosystem and which will enter into force by 2012 In the European context, I see both institutional and economic developments. From an institutional point of view, I will admit that the Constitutional Treaty has been adopted and has entered into force. This means that in the future the integration of institutions, markets and infrastructures will have been strengthened, but also that European integration will have progressed in areas such as justice and defence or external representation. The European Union should then have 27 members after the accession of Romania and Bulgaria. The EU's other neighbouring countries are likely to have signed enhanced cooperation contracts. As for economic developments, I will also assume that what has been said and promised will be done. I am thinking in particular of the opening up and Europeanisation of the energy, telecommunications and banking markets. I also assume that in the rail and road sectors, the European dimension and interconnection will have been improved, which should lead to greater mobility within the European Union, like the mobility achieved in the education sector with the recognition of diplomas. On the other hand, the regions are likely to have a stronger economic role by then. For the moment, only one point of importance creates uncertainty: the question of the new European budget, which has still not been settled. Secondly, within the framework of the Eurosystem, I estimate according to the announced plans that there will be 22 countries that adopted the euro in 2012, calculating that England, Sweden and Denmark will not have wished to introduce it and that Bulgaria and Romania will not yet be ready by that date. This will have an impact on the organisation of voting rights in the Governing Council. This body, which defines the monetary policy of the euro area, consists of the governors of the national central banks of the euro area and the 6 members of the Executive Board of the ECB. In 2012, this will make a total of 28 members. Within the Governing Council, the principle of "one man, one vote" is required. At the beginning of 2003, only a change in the frequency of voting was decided with a view to expanding the Governing Council. The aim of this amendment was to preserve in the future the Governing Council's ability to take decisions effectively and quickly in an enlarged euro area. By 20012, a system of rotation of voting periods among Governors sitting on the Governing Council will be put in place. The 22 governors will be divided into three groups. In each group, an egalitarian rotation will be carried out so that each governor can vote at a reasonable frequency. Thanks to the importance of Luxembourg's financial centre, the BCL should be part of the second group (9 governors). However, this is not the only development that the Eurosystem will undergo between now and 2012. The discussion will be determined by the search for balance: Between centralization and decentralization or concentration and deconcentration (specialization) Between European and national competences (principle of subsidiarity) Between tasks assigned to the Eurosystem and their interactions with those carried out by other institutions such as the Council of Ministers or the Commission, e.g. in relation to financial stability or public deficits. In practice, this may be tantamount to resolving the question of whether tenders for computer equipment should  and can  be made jointly or not. A very important topic will soon be discussed. Indeed, the distribution of monetary income as it is provided for today is valid until 2007 and will have to be renegotiated. Thirdly, and to close this section on my assumptions about the future, a number of operational decisions have already been taken by the Eurosystem in the direction of cohesion and efficiency gains. Their implementation lasts from 2005 to 2015. They concern all areas, such as: Banknote production Reserve management Guarantees accepted to give credit to banks A common platform to transfer large payments A more user-friendly environment for transfers, direct debits, transfers electronics, credit cards Better statistical information A more active role for the Eurosystem in the legislative process and in financial stability Etc. As you can see, a lot of work is underway and in 2012 the Eurosystem will not have quite the same face as in 2005. And yet, as of today, we can already see how far we have come since the introduction of the euro. The evolution of the BCL's missions The BCL was created on 1 June 1998, at the same time as the ECB. Until then, Luxembourg did not have a central bank and the creation of the BCL was done on the basis of the Luxembourg Monetary Institute. From the outset, the BCL's main task has been to participate in the performance of the Eurosystem's tasks. It also carries out the tasks entrusted by its own organic law or by other laws, regulations or conventions. The BCL has always operated at both a supranational level, that of the euro area, and at a national level. I cannot therefore speak about the evolution of the BCL's tasks, let alone the tasks of the Eurosystem. Participate in Eurosystem missions The Eurosystem, composed of the NCBs of the countries that have adopted the euro and the ECB, has several fundamental tasks established by the Maastricht Treaty: the definition and implementation of monetary policy, the conduct of foreign exchange operations, the holding and management of the official foreign exchange reserves of the Member States, as well as promoting the proper functioning of payment systems. In addition, it contributes to the sound conduct of the policies pursued by the competent authorities with regard to the prudential supervision of credit institutions and the stability of the financial system. It also collects the statistical information necessary for the performance of its tasks and the issue of banknotes in the euro area. It is therefore in these missions that the BCL must participate. They are multiple, but the main objective is unique: price stability. However, without prejudice to the main objective, the Eurosystem also supports the general economic policies of the Community, of which growth is one of the objectives. Price stability is an essential objective in the missions of any modern central bank, but is not classified in the same way in each central bank. While it is the main objective of the Eurosystem, in the United States for example, it is considered on an equal footing by the Federal Reserve System with the objective of maximum employment and moderate long-term rates. So why did you choose such an approach? Because price stability is a public good! To put it simply: 1. In an environment of price stability, the market is able to allocate resources efficiently. Indeed, price variability complicates the evaluation of prices. This uncertainty increases the probability of errors by economic agents. For example, price comparison becomes more difficult and one may not buy a product at the best price. 2. It is also important to limit monetary erosion (i.e. the loss of value of money) in order to maintain the purchasing power of economic agents, which promotes consumption, investment and in turn growth and employment. In linking our main objective with support for the Community's general economic policies, it should be stressed that price stability and support for the real economy should not be regarded as exclusive but, on the contrary, complementary. Indeed, as I have just explained, price stability is the best contribution in the medium term to sustainable and job-creating growth. Maintaining price stability, by avoiding unnecessary volatility, helps to create favourable conditions for growth and employment. On the other hand, many economists have shown that the setting of secondary objectives has negative consequences from the point of view of their feasibility in practice and also from the point of view of considerations of an economic nature. In the long run, there is no trade-off between inflation and growth. Indeed: 1. This trade-off exists in the short term, but in the long term generates more inflation, without additional growth and employment. 2. While monetary policy inflections are having a short-term effect on overall output in the euro area, output will eventually return to a level very close to its initial level. 3. The impact of monetary policy on prices is more moderate in the short term, but persists over time. Any temptation to use monetary policy in the short term should therefore be avoided. By the way: It is for this reason that monetary policy must be entrusted to an independent central bank, since the political powers, in search of short-term votes in the electoral deadlines, can more easily give in to this temptation. Finally, I would like to stress that inflation has a cost: 1. Investment tends to go to the financial sector and to assets that neutralize the effects of inflation instead of towards production. 2. It has a fiscal cost for all taxpayers, because wages follow its evolution and even more so in a country like Luxembourg where wage indexation still exists. By increasing the nominal income of taxpayers, it increases everyone's tax rate as part of a progressive tax rate that is not indexed with the same regularity. What is gained on one side is therefore lost on the other. I just mentioned that the independence of central banks was a good thing. It should be noted, however, that this independence is not without compensation. Central banks must practice transparency and be accountable to democratically elected bodies, but also to the general public. In particular, in order to enable the public to better assess the performance of the Eurosystem in carrying out this task, the Governing Council of the ECB decided to define price stability. Since 2003, this has been defined over the medium term as corresponding to inflation below, but close to, 2% for the euro area as a whole. The fact that price stability is defined in relation to the euro area as a whole means that the Governing Council does not act on the basis of inflation rates in individual countries. As for the medium-term perspective, as I have explained, it underlines that monetary policy has no short-term effects on prices. I would add that it should be noted that the impact of a change in the official interest rate on prices is done with a lag in time of an average of 12 to 18 months. The Governing Council assesses risks to price stability on the basis of two pillars. The first pillar includes a long-term monetary analysis and aims, in short, to monitor the growth of the quantity of money, as this is closely linked to the issue of inflation. The second pillar of the strategy is the analysis of a wide range of economic and financial indicators that can provide information on future price developments. To achieve its objective, a central bank does not exert a direct influence on prices, but rather on interest rates. Some call this the "rent of money." The single monetary policy is thus based on the setting of the level of the short-term interest rate and the volume of liquidity granted to credit institutions and, in turn, to individuals and the economy as a whole. Indeed, the change in the interest rate applied to commercial banks, decided by the Governing Council of the ECB, has an impact on the conditions offered to their own customers. While decisions on rates are centralised at the level of the Governing Council, the execution of decisions is decentralised at the level of the national central banks, the latter together forming the operational arm of the Eurosystem on an equal footing. This is where the BCL's participation in the Eurosystem's tasks begins. In this context, the BCL carries out operations on the financial markets (open market operations). This means, in practice, that it grants credit to credit institutions in the Luxembourg financial centre that need them. As collateral, it receives securities on deposit. To put it very simply, the rate of these loans granted to commercial banks is set once a month by the Governing Council. If the rate is high, economic agents will ask for less credit and if it is low, they will ask for more. The Governing Council can therefore curb or accelerate the demand for money in this way. The BCL also has a regulatory instrument which consists in requiring credit institutions to hold minimum reserves with the BCL. By increasing or decreasing the amount of these minimum reserves, the ECB and the national central banks influence the need for credit institutions to refinance themselves, i.e. to apply for credit, from their national central banks. These monetary policy operations within the Eurosystem are carried by a payment system called TARGET. This system currently consists of an interconnection of national real-time gross settlement systems. In Luxembourg, this national system is called LIPS-Gross. The BCL monitors developments in existing systems as well as the execution of payments. With the arrival of TARGET2 in 2007, national central banks will no longer have to manage their own large payment systems. They will be able to make use of a shareable platform. However, each national central bank will preserve the relationship with "its" own participants. Sharing technical infrastructure will allow for service harmonization and cost reduction through economies of scale. In financial markets, and even more so in the context of monetary policy operations, payment systems are inseparable from clearing and securities settlement systems. The settlement of securities transactions involves two flows: delivery of securities and payment. While initially, the delivery of securities was done in a physical form, the vast majority is now done in a dematerialized way, in the form of accounting entries. Securities are located with central securities depositories. The securities given as collateral by the banks to the BCL are thus deposited with Clearstream. That said, banks cannot give any security as collateral. So far, each national central bank has drawn up a list of securities that it is prepared to accept as a security deposit. To simplify this system, the central banks of the countries that have adopted the euro are trying to agree on a single list for the entire Eurosystem. This is also more in the spirit of European integration. Central banks are also concerned about financial stability. It must be noted that this is inseparable from price stability. Price stability, by anchoring agents' expectations, contributes to financial stability. Conversely, financial instability can undermine price stability. Thus, for example, an exchange rate crisis can lead to a depreciation of the exchange rate and generate imported inflation. The Eurosystem's stability mandate is twofold: contribute the policies pursued by the competent bodies in the field of prudential supervision of credit institutions and the stability of the financial system; and promote the smooth operation of payment systems. This involvement of central banks in financial stability is justified by 3 arguments: 1. The combination of the money-making role of central banks and the participation of commercial banks in this money-creating process 2. Cash held by commercial banks accounts for a large portion of total liquidity; and 3. Central banks need to verify the quality of their counterparties, not only because they deal with them, but also to ensure the proper functioning of the financial system. The BCL has therefore set up macroprudential indicators to monitor the overall evolution of the Luxembourg financial system. During the first six months of its existence, the BCL even incorporated the activity of micro-prudential supervision, i.e. individual financial institutions. The law then entrusted this supervision to the Financial Sector Supervisory Commission. Luxembourg is the only country in the European Union where this separation leads to a total lack of bilateral coordination between micro-prudential and macro-prudential supervision. This institutional configuration has created an unpremeditated situation where financial stability no longer assumes the status of a public good, against the current of financial globalization in general and further reducing Luxembourg's low weight on the international scene. As we have seen, payment systems like TARGET2 allow payments to be made securely and on time. They thus contribute to good economic development and contribute to financial stability. Symmetrically, they are a significant source of financial instability. Because of the size of the amounts channelled through them, a default by a counterparty can cause a domino effect qualified as systemic risk. The legislator has conferred the supervision of this in principle on the CSSF and by exception on the BCL. In the context of the payment systems in which it participates, the BCL has always ensured that the systems comply with the international standards and recommendations in force. The issuance and circulation of currency signs is another task of the Eurosystem in which the BCL participates. Traditionally, money performs the functions of means of payment, store of value and unit of account. The euro was put into cash circulation in 2002. This form implicitly embodies an essential element inherent in money: trust, necessary for the acceptance of a currency. Thus, central banks have a primary function to play in the construction and maintenance of capital confidence linked to a currency: Warrant low monetary erosion in order to guarantee the purchasing power of a currency; Warrant the quality and incorporation of good security features in banknotes in order to promote their longevity and ensure protection against counterfeiting and; Insure an adequate supply of monetary signs to the economy. The first imperative is, as we have seen, the main objective of the Eurosystem. The security features are the result of sophisticated techniques and make the euro at least as secure a banknote as the safest of the banknotes that have previously circulated in the national monetary areas. The BCL issues and puts into circulation the euro banknotes, but only puts the coins into circulation, on behalf of and in the name of the State Treasury, the issuance of which is the responsibility of the latter to date. The BCL also plays an essential role in the collection of statistics, which is indispensable in the strategy as well as in the execution of monetary policy. For example, the BCL compiles national data from the broad monetary indicator. These data are then aggregated at the euro area level and form the analytical basis of the first pillar of the monetary policy strategy. It also collects and provides a large number of economic and financial statistics to the Eurosystem, used under the second pillar. In the context of monetary policy, the calculation and monitoring of the minimum reserves to be set up by counterparties with the BCL is essential. The BCL's national missions In addition to its Tasks related to the Eurosystem, the BCL also has a number of tasks at national level. To extend the issue of statistics, the BCL produces statistics on the financial centre, the use of which is essentially confined to a national level. In addition, the BCL was instructed by the legislator to set up, together with STATEC, Luxembourg's balance of payments. Beyond a simple statistical record of the economic transactions of an economic zone with the rest of the world, the balance of payments is of major interest for the economic policy of a country. The BCL, like any central bank, has a research department. As such, it participates in the national economic debate. Its independence allows it to make analyses without being subjected to political pressure. In Luxembourg, these studies are the only ones that are carried out on a regular basis and thus feed into the country's current economic debates. The BCL's involvement also covers two other areas: technical assistance and the provision of services to central banks outside the ESCB and to international and even supranational institutions. In terms of financial services, BCL offers its expertise in reserve management for the same categories of institutions. Finally, as an institution rooted in the Luxembourg financial landscape, the BCL is keen to closely involve economic actors. In order to establish a dialogue, the BCL has set up various working committees which it organizes, particularly in the fields of statistics, market operations, payment systems, etc. All these activities, both European and national, should evolve by 2012 according to the evolution of the frameworks that I presented to you at the beginning of my speech. However, this development is not a foregone conclusion and the Governing Council remains vigilant. I am now at your disposal for any questions you may have and thank you for your attention.

Title: The conditions for the success of capital account liberalization
text: THE CONDITIONS FOR THE SUCCESS OF CAPITAL ACCOUNT LIBERALIZATION Speech by Mr Yves Mersch, President of the BCL Meeting of French-speaking central banks  Marrakech, 9-12 May 2005 Only the word spoken is authentic Recent financial history has been marked by the resurgence of financial crises, particularly affecting countries newly integrated into international financial movements. The costs associated with these crises and the risks they pose to the global economy due to contagion phenomena have revived the debate on the effects of capital account liberalization on growth, both in academic and political circles. Theoretically, the case for liberalization is mainly based on several ideas: one more efficient allocation of resources, thus promoting lower costs of capital and thus investment, one better diversification of risks, with wider access to financial markets making it possible to better diversify the portfolio of assets and thus reduce the volatility of consumption, the development of the domestic financial sector. The emergence of new instruments and techniques, as well as the opening up of the market to foreign players, should increase competition and thus increase the efficiency of the financial system as a whole. Nevertheless, the existence of imperfections and the risks associated with movements in financial markets, especially if they are speculative, condition the positive effects that can be expected from liberalization. Moreover, the existence of a positive relationship between the liberalization of capital movements and growth is difficult to demonstrate empirically. It seems that liberalization is not a sufficient condition for growth and that other factors must be taken into account. The attitude of the IMF, which now seems to be more systematically warning of the risks associated with too rapid and uncontrolled liberalization of the capital account, testifies to the evolution of the positions of the international community on this subject. Academic and political developments favour rather the idea that the opening of the capital account will be all the more beneficial if it is implemented gradually and conditional on certain reforms. The purpose of this intervention is to feed the debate on this issue and to clarify some proposals that could promote the success of the liberalization of the capital account. Conditioning the liberalization of the capital account -At the forefront of the conditions for the successful opening of the capital account is undoubtedly the development and stability of the financial system and the establishment of an effective system of regulation and prudential supervision. It is indeed important to strengthen the capacity of the financial system to cope with macroeconomic and financial shocks at the same time. The establishment of micro and macroprudential arrangements should thus contribute to increasing the resilience of the banking and financial system. The objective here is to reduce the vulnerability of the financial system, to prevent contagion from endangering the whole system when an operator experiences difficulties, to increase the capacity of the system as a whole to absorb macroeconomic shocks and to avoid excessive exposure to risks. However, it can also be argued that the gradual opening of the capital account is likely to promote the emergence of reliable and effective institutions and modes of regulation. The vast majority of European countries maintained restrictions on their financial systems as well as controls on the foreign exchange market before gradually liberalizing, first the domestic financial system and then the capital account. For example, the reform of the French banking system was not carried out until the mid-1980s, while restrictions on the foreign exchange market were lifted in 1989. The case of the Luxembourg economy, on the other hand, is particular in that the development of a strong financial centre has been, among other things, favoured by the existence of more restrictive legislation in most neighbouring countries. On the contrary, it is therefore here an early and complete opening that has allowed economic and financial development since Luxembourg banks, relying on the tradition of banking secrecy and the absence of restrictions on capital movements, have taken advantage of more restrictive regulations in the United States and other European countries to impose themselves on the Euro-currency market. It should be stressed here that the existence of a stable political climate and the dual foreign exchange market established within the framework of the Belgian-Luxembourg monetary association played an essential role. A distinction was made between the regulated market on which transactions included in the current account were processed and on which the franc was pegged to the dollar under the Bretton Woods agreements, first in the context of the monetary snake and the European Monetary System (EMS); in contrast, the other market segment, known as the free market, saw the operations of the financial account unravelled. This system lasted from 1955 to 1990, thus guaranteeing the stability of the exchange rate in current operations and allowing the financial franc to adjust freely on the other market. The historical experience of the dual foreign exchange market was therefore very positive, allowing the first liberalization of capital movements in post-war Europe, while sheltering foreign exchange reserves. The room for manoeuvre it allowed was welcome, especially when it was not needed, as the experience of a deep divergence between these two markets during the period following the first and second oil shocks has amply documented. -The question of the exchange rate regime is thus at the heart of the problem of the success of the opening of the capital account. It should be recalled, however, that in some cases fixed exchange rate regimes have proved particularly fragile as a result of the liberalization of capital movements; the most striking examples are undoubtedly the EMS crisis in 1992, despite the gradual liberalisation undertaken by the European countries, the Asian countries in 1997 and 1998 and Brazil in 1999. The collapse of the Argentine currency board has also called into question the sustainability of so-called "hard" exchange rate regimes. In addition, recent financial crises, regularly referred to as "twin crises", have often involved the foreign exchange and bank credit markets. This is why the IMF now seems to be encouraging the implementation of greater exchange rate flexibility. Nevertheless, the risks associated with this type of diet are less known. It is mainly for political and institutional reasons that the European countries have maintained a fixed but adjustable exchange rate regime (even after the collapse of the Bretton Woods system) even if it means establishing a dual foreign exchange market as we have just seen in Belgium and Luxembourg. However, the existence of this dual market has not always made it possible to protect itself from the pressures exerted on the foreign exchange market. Thus, the increasing overvaluation of the regulated franc, mainly due to the increase in Belgian public debt, forced the authorities to devalue in 1982. -In addition, the issues of the choice of exchange rate regime and the opening of the capital account cannot be separated from that of the macroeconomic policies that are pursued. It is generally considered difficult to maintain simultaneously a fixed exchange rate regime, full freedom of capital movements and the independence of monetary policy. The objective of monetary policy must therefore necessarily be compatible with the choice of exchange rate regime and the desire to open the capital account. Fiscal policy is also important, even central, since fears about the sustainability of this policy can lead to widespread mistrust and accelerate capital flight, which puts the exchange rate regime in difficulty. These problems are of a general nature but especially thorny in countries that are heavily dollarized (or Euroized) and whose debt is contracted in the short term. -More generally, the quality and stability of the legal, institutional and political frameworks are essential aspects of economic development. All these elements contribute to the establishment of good governance and are therefore a condition for the successful liberalization of capital movements. Problems of corruption and collusion are a brake on investment and do not allow for a truly efficient allocation of resources. These policies must also be accompanied by greater transparency of information, thus reducing information asymmetries and thus better risk assessment. A sequential approach to opening the capital account In this second part, the aim is to show that it may be preferable to carry out a gradual liberalisation of capital movements. Inevitably, all the conditions mentioned above are all steps that are likely to precede or at least accompany the opening of the capital account. Thus, the conditional approach goes hand in hand with a sequential approach and it is an all-encompassing vision of the issue that takes precedence. -The opening of the current account can probably not be considered as long as there are restrictions on the domestic level. Otherwise, all domestic regulations quickly become inoperative to the extent that they can be circumvented. It does indeed seem more coherent to first strengthen the competitiveness of the banking and financial system by liberalizing the domestic market. However, this competition must undoubtedly be done gradually at the risk of destabilizing an economic system that would not have had time to adapt to the new competitive environment. The management of the risks inherent in this new environment is indeed the result of learning and the implementation of effective internal procedures. Accelerated liberalization in a still fragile environment would expose the banking and financial system to an increased risk of crisis. This is how the majority of European countries proceeded during the 1970s and 1980s. -The opening of the current account must probably precede that of the capital account. The main reason being that the opening of the capital account has all the more positive effects as the real economy is already open. Moreover, it seems that while the benefits of capital liberalization are still uncertain, the effects of trade integration are much less questioned. -Finally, it is certainly necessary to gradually liberalise the various capital movements according to the beneficial effects they may have on the economy and also taking into account the risks they are likely to produce on financial stability. The positive effects of direct investment on growth are indeed recognized. Conversely, the risks of destabilizing effects of portfolio investments and bank capital are higher, the volatility of portfolio investments being indeed much greater than that of direct investments. In recent episodes of financial crises, the speed with which capital has left the country has often been impressive. These reversals result not only from the potentially unstable nature of portfolio investments but also from the often short-term structure of both private and public debt. Also, in order to mitigate the destabilizing effects of these reversals on the financial markets, it is beneficial to promote longer-term debt and in the domestic currency so as not to amplify the fluctuations in the price of a security by that of the exchange rate, which too often contributes to calling into question its repayment. Yet fostering such a type of indebtedness is not the result of political will alone, but is largely the result of a combination of a series of factors: first, structural measures aimed at strengthening a competitive banking sector and effective intermediation through capital markets; secondly, a monetary policy whose main purpose is to maintain the purchasing power of money, so that financial instruments denominated in national currency are sought after and used for long-term indebtedness and investment; finally, a sustainable fiscal policy that is a prerequisite so that the public sector can play a leading role through its own securities issuances and that the public finance situation does not exert inhibiting influences on local markets and financial instruments. Conclusion It is probably difficult to prioritize the various arguments that have just been put forward. Similarly, it remains difficult to state with certainty that such an aspect is a determining factor in the success of the opening of the current account. Nevertheless, the objective was probably more to show that the issue of liberalization is not independent of a set of other issues and that liberalization should only take place within the framework of a thoughtful and coherent policy. It therefore seems necessary to take into account the specific economic situation of the country exchange rate before embarking on a capital account liberalization programme in order to assess the benefits and risks inherent in the approach. It is indeed a question on which it is undoubtedly necessary to free oneself from all dogma. Any schematic and one-size-fits-all approach must then be excluded in order to take account of the sectoral and geographical economic structures of countries wishing to embark on the path of liberalization of capital movements. Finally, it must be borne in mind that liberalization cannot be an end in itself but must be adopted pragmatically to the extent that it promotes growth and development. It has undoubtedly been the tool in Luxembourg, but conversely, the sustainability of controls in other countries may have made it possible to strengthen the banking system in order to better prepare it for an intensification of competition and thus avoid an economic and financial crisis.

Il faut nanmoins rappeler que dans certains cas, les rgimes de changes fixes se sont rvls particulirement fragiles  la suite de la libralisation des mouvements de capitaux ; les exemples les plus marquants tant sans doute : la crise du SME en 1992, malgr une libralisation progressive entreprise par les pays europens, les pays asiatiques en 1997 et 1998 ou encore le Brsil en 1999. Par ailleurs, les crises financires rcentes qualifies rgulirement de  crises jumelles  ont souvent impliqu les marchs des changes et du crdit bancaire. Cest pourquoi le FMI semble aujourdhui plutt encourager la mise en uvre dune plus grande flexibilit des changes. Nanmoins, les risques associs  ce type de rgimes sont moins connus. Cest essentiellement pour des raisons politiques et institutionnelles que les pays europens ont maintenu un rgime de changes fixes mais ajustables (mme aprs leffondrement du systme de Bretton-Woods) quitte  instaurer un double march des changes comme nous venons de le voir en Belgique et au Luxembourg. Pour autant, lexistence de ce march dual na pas toujours permis de se mettre  labri des pressions exerces sur le march des changes. Ainsi, la survaluation grandissante du franc rglement, due principalement  laugmentation de la dette publique belge, a contraint les autorits  la dvaluation en 1982. -En outre, les questions du choix du rgime de changes et de louverture du compte de capital ne peuvent tre spares de celle des politiques macroconomiques qui sont menes. On considre gnralement quil est difficile de maintenir simultanment un rgime de changes fixes, une libert totale des mouvements de capitaux et lindpendance de la politique montaire. Lobjectif de la politique montaire doit donc tre ncessairement compatible avec le choix du rgime de changes et la volont douvrir le compte de capital. La politique budgtaire est galement importante, voire centrale, puisque des craintes pesant sur la soutenabilit de cette politique peuvent tre  lorigine dune dfiance gnralise et acclrer la fuite des capitaux mettant en difficult le rgime de changes. Ces problmes sont de nature gnrale mais surtout pineux dans les pays fortement dollariss (ou euroiss) et dont lendettement est contract  court terme. -Plus gnralement, la qualit et la stabilit des cadres juridique, institutionnel et politique sont des aspects essentiels du dveloppement conomique. Tous ces lments participent en effet de la mise en place dune bonne gouvernance et constituent donc une condition du succs de la libralisation des mouvements de capitaux. Les problmes de corruption et de collusion sont un frein pour linvestissement et ne permettent pas une allocation vraiment efficace des ressources. Ces politiques doivent par ailleurs tre accompagnes par une plus grande transparence de linformation permettant ainsi de rduire les asymtries dinformation et donc une meilleure valuation des risques. Une approche squentielle de louverture du compte de capital Dans cette seconde partie, lobjectif est de monter quil peut tre prfrable de procder  une libralisation progressive des mouvements de capitaux. Ncessairement, toutes les conditions voques prcdemment sont autant dtapes qui sont susceptibles de prcder ou du moins daccompagner louverture du compte de capital. Ainsi, lapproche conditionnelle va de pair avec une approche squentielle et cest une vision englobante de la question qui prime. -Louverture du compte courant ne peut sans doute pas tre envisage tant quil existe des restrictions sur le plan domestique. Autrement, toutes les rglementations domestiques deviennent rapidement inoprantes dans la mesure o elles peuvent tre contournes. Il semble effectivement plus cohrent de renforcer dabord la comptitivit du systme bancaire et financier en libralisant le march domestique. Toutefois, cette mise en concurrence doit sans doute se faire progressivement au risque de dstabiliser un systme conomique qui naurait pas eu le temps de sadapter au nouvel environnement concurrentiel. La gestion des risques inhrents  ce nouvel environnement est en effet le rsultat dun apprentissage et de la mise en place de procdures internes efficaces. Une libralisation prcipite dans un environnement encore fragile exposerait le systme bancaire et financier  un risque accru de crise. Cest ainsi quont procds la majorit des pays europens au cours des annes 1970 et 1980. -Louverture du compte courant doit sans doute prcder celle du compte de capital. La raison principale tant que louverture du compte de capital a des effets dautant plus positifs que lconomie relle est dj ouverte. Il semble de surcrot que si les bienfaits de la libralisation des mouvements de capitaux sont encore incertains, les effets de lintgration commerciale sont beaucoup moins remis en cause -Enfin, il convient certainement de libraliser progressivement les diffrents mouvements de capitaux en fonction des effets bnfiques quils peuvent avoir sur lconomie et aussi en prenant en compte les risques quils sont susceptibles de produire sur la stabilit financire. Les effets positifs des investissements directs sur la croissance sont effectivement reconnus. A linverse les risques deffets dstabilisants des investissements de portefeuille et des capitaux bancaires sont plus levs, la volatilit des investissements de portefeuille tant effectivement bien plus importante que celle des investissements directs. Lors des pisodes rcents de crises financires, la rapidit avec laquelle les capitaux sont sortis du pays a t souvent impressionnante. Ces retournements rsultent non seulement du caractre potentiellement instable des investissements de portefeuille mais galement de la structure bien souvent  court terme de lendettement tant priv que public. Aussi, afin dattnuer les effets dstabilisants de ces retournements sur les marchs financiers, il est bnfique de favoriser un endettement  plus long terme et dans la devise domestique afin de ne pas amplifier les fluctuations du prix dun titre par celle du taux de change, ce qui trop souvent concourt  remettre en cause son remboursement. Pourtant favoriser un tel type dendettement ne procde pas de la seule volont politique, mais est largement le rsultat de la conjonction dune srie de facteurs: dabord, de mesures structurelles visant  fortifier un secteur bancaire concurrentiel et une intermdiation efficace par les marchs des capitaux ; ensuite, dune politique montaire ayant comme finalit principale le maintien du pouvoir dachat de la monnaie, afin que les instruments financiers libells en monnaie nationale soient recherchs et utiliss pour des endettements et investissements  long terme ; finalement, dune politique budgtaire soutenable qui est un pr-requis afin que le secteur public puisse le cas chant jouer un rle moteur au travers de ses propres missions de titres et que la situation en matire de finances publiques nexerce pas dinfluences inhibitrices sur les marchs et instruments financiers locaux. Conclusion Il est sans doute difficile de hirarchiser les diffrents arguments qui viennent dtre exposs. De mme, quil reste dlicat daffirmer avec certitude que tel aspect est un lment dterminant du succs de louverture du compte courant. Nanmoins, lobjectif tait sans doute plus de montrer que la question de la libralisation nest pas indpendante dun ensemble dautres questions et que cette libralisation ne doit se faire que dans le cadre dune politique rflchie et cohrente. Il semble ainsi ncessaire de prendre en compte la situation conomique spcifique de change pays avant de sengager dans un programme de libralisation du compte de capital afin dvaluer les avantages et les risques inhrents  la dmarche. Cest effectivement une question sur laquelle il est sans doute ncessaire de saffranchir de tout dogme. Toute approche schmatique et unique doit alors tre exclue de faon  prendre en compte les structures conomiques sectorielles et gographiques des pays qui souhaitent sengager sur la voie de la libralisation des mouvements de capitaux. Finalement, il faut garder  lesprit que la libralisation ne peut tre une fin en soi mais quelle doit tre adopte de faon pragmatique dans la mesure o elle permet de favoriser la croissance et le dveloppement. Elle en a sans doute t loutil au Luxembourg mais inversement, la prennit des contrles dans dautres pays a peut-tre permis de renforcer le systme bancaire afin de mieux le prparer  une intensification de la concurrence et viter ainsi une crise conomique et financire.

Title: In the focus of the European Central Bank
text: The spoken word is valid Embargo: 10h00 CEST, 9. September 2005 Yves Mersch Chairman of the Banque centrale du Luxembourg In the focus of the European Central Bank 1 The spoken word is valid Dear Sir or Madam, I am very pleased to be able to contribute to the Capital Markets Forum 2005 today and I would like to thank WGZ-Bank Luxembourg for the invitation. I would like to use the time available tome to explain to you the challenges of the Eurosystem's monetary policy from today's perspective and to discuss recent ECB decisions. As you probably already know, at the beginning of September the Governing Council of the ECB decided again to leave the key interest rates of the Eurosystem unchanged. The latter have been at an unusually low level for more than two years now. In August, hardly any economic development caused as much excitement as the rising oil prices, which lastmonth again set new records. Hurricane Katrina devastated parts of the southern coast of the USA and caused several refineries to be inoperable now and probably in the near future. The rise in oil prices is not without impact on economic growth. This is therefore also reflected in the current Eurosystem projections: the projections for real economic growth are 1.0 to 1.6 percent for 2005 and 1.3 to 2.3 percent for 2006. The projections for real economic growth are thus similar to the expectations of other organisations and have declined somewhat compared to June; this reflects both a revision of growth in the first quarter of 2005and higher oil prices. In the second quarter 2 The spoken word applies In 2005, according to Eurostat's forecast, real gross domestic product in the euro area grew by 0.3% quarter-on-quarter, a slight decrease of 0.1 percentage points compared withthe previous quarter and equivalent to about 1.2% on an annualised basis. The latest economic indicators for the euro area therefore confirm continued subdued growth. The rise in oil prices is also having a negative impact on purchasing power and consumerconfidence. Although the ZEW Index on the general economic situation has risen significantly in recent months, the European Commission's Consumer Confidence Indicator has not improved noticeably. Rather, according to the latest data, it reached its lowest level since May last year. Trade sales decreased very slightly in the second quarter of 2005 compared to the previous quarter, after an increase of 0.8% in the first quarter; Bycontrast, with growth of 1.9%, the number of new passenger car registrations is on the rise. It should be noted that the combined contribution of retail trade and car registrations together accounts for about 45% of private consumption in the euro area. However, weak domestic demand in the euro area continues to contrast with continued growth in global demand. As far as price developments are concerned, the rise in oil prices has had a major impact on producer prices: while the annualrate of inflation of the 3 Producer price index (excluding construction) was 3.5% in May 2005, while inflation was 4.0% in June and July 2005. Eurostat's annual inflation forecast of theHarmonized Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) was 2.1% in August, a slight decrease compared with the previous month. As oil prices rise, we expect the annual inflation rate to fluctuate around these levels over the next few months. The Eurosystem projections show that the annual inflation rate will be between 2.1% and 2.3% in 2005 and between 1.4% and 2.4% in 2006. High oil prices have raised inflation expectations for the coming year, which is why these estimatesare considerably higher than in June this year (1.8 to 2.2 percent in 2005 and 0.9 to 2.1 percent in 2006). According to these developments, it is of paramount importance to avoid possible second-round effects in wage and price formation, which pose the main risk to the inflation outlook. It is therefore important that the social partners continue to assume their responsibilities. Consequently, the Governing Council will continue to monitor developments in this regard with ongoing vigilance to ensure that longer-term inflation expectations in the euro area remain anchored at levels consistent with price stability. Firmly anchored inflation expectations are alsoof particular importance for investment markets. Rising oil prices worsen growth prospects and 4 It is true that the spoken word increases inflationary pressures; this in turn leads market participants to revise their interest rate expectations. A possibleslowdown in economic growth may result in market participants revising their interest rate expectations downwards, while higher inflation expectations may lead to an upward revision of interest rate expectations. It is therefore only with firmly anchoredinflation expectations that it is possible to avoid an upward revision of government yields in times of constantly rising oil prices. As a result of the rise in oil prices, the downward trend in long-term interest rates in the euro area therefore continued during August. At the end of the month, ten-year government bond yields reached their lowest level in the history of the Eurosystem; long-term interest rates were just under 3.1% in the euro area, while they werearound 4.0% in the US. As a result, the yield differential between ten-year government bonds in the United States and the euro area, which fell below its monthly average of around 100 basis points at the end of August, has also widened. It would certainly be an exaggeration to attribute the downward trend in yields since mid-2004 entirely to the monetary policy decisions of the European Central Bank. Nevertheless, it is important to stress that the low ten-year government bond yields are due, at least in part, to firmly anchored inflation expectations. By firmly anchoring inflation expectations within the framework of price stability, monetary policy contributes to the 5 The spoken word European Central Bank alsocontributes to a revival of economic growth. But it is not only long-term government bond yields that have fallen, as the yield curve has continued to flatten over the past few weeks (this applies to both the euro currency exchangerate and the US). At the end of last month, the yield differential between two- and ten-year government bonds in the euro area reached 90 basis points, while the yield differential between five- and ten-year bonds reached 57 basis points. Because low government bond yields serve as a discount factor for equities, they contribute to a positive performance in equity prices, although the rise in oil prices in August did not spare equity markets either. In the euro area in particular, prices had recorded strong increases until the beginning of August thanks to the goodearnings situation of companies. The Dow Jones Euro STOXX index is up more than 13% year-to-date, while the Standard & Poor's 500 index and the Nikkei 225 are up just 0.8% and 8.9%, respectively. In August, however, the euroarea and the US fell by more than one percent, while the Japanese index rose by almost 4% thanks to the release of favourable economic data. As already mentioned, the dynamic development of oil prices has not only driven down yields on long-term government bonds and negatively impacted consumer confidence. 6 Market participants also fear that the rise in oil prices worldwide could lead to a revision of growth forecasts. These fears, reinforced by the scale of disasters in the US, also had an impact on the euro-dollar exchange rate. Although interest rateand currency differentials have widened, sentiment towards the US currency has continued to deteriorate. As a result, the dollar has depreciated by around 3% against the euro since July. The dollar thus lost some of the appreciation recorded in the first half of the year. Until the beginning of July, the euro had continued its downward movement against the American dollar, which had been evident since the beginning of the year. But even at the end of August, the euro was only slightly above the average oflast year. Furthermore, recent developments in the euro-dollar exchange rate are due to the publication of the latest euro area balance of payments data. The latest data point to a very strong increase in net capitalinflows in portfolio investment, so that market participants are likely to continue to pay more attention to these data. It should be noted that although the euro has appreciated against the dollar over the past month, this appreciation has been offset to some extent by the depreciation of the euro against other currencies. Despite some price fluctuations, the nominal effective euro exchange rate remained close to 7 The spoken word remains unchanged. In thefirst few months of this year, the nominal effective euro exchange rate depreciated by 5.7%. The real effective euro exchange rate also depreciated markedly during the year, reflecting an improvement in the competitiveness of the euro area's exports. So far, my contribution has been limited to the economic situation in the euro area. However, as you know, the European Central Bank distinguishes between economic and monetary analysis. While the former is limited to theassessment of risks to price stability in the short to medium term, the latter refers to the medium to longer term. Monetary analysis is therefore essential for monetary policy. Since the second half of2004, we have seen a steady increase in monetary growth in the euro area. After annual growth of the broad monetary aggregate M3 of approximately 5.4% in the second quarter of 2004, the average growth rate of M3 was 7.2% in the second quarter of 2005. The latest figures for July 2005 point to a continuation of this trend, with money supply growth in this month being a seasonally adjusted 7.9%. The results of the monetary analysis show that the high annual growth of M3 continues to be driven mainly by the growth rate included in the monetary aggregate M1. 8 The spoken word liquid instruments apply. In July this year, the annual growth rate of the narrow monetary aggregateM1 rose to 11.1%. The liquid instruments contained in M1 thus already contribute around 4.5 percentage points to the growth of M3. Recent figures point to continued high growth in both currency in circulation and overnight deposits. The brisk demand for cash is largely due to the adjustment process initiated by the introduction of euro cash. At this stage, however, it cannot be ruled out that this process will eventually converge into a higherdemand for cash. Model-based analyses also indicate that the persistently high demand for overnight deposits is largely due to the low level of interest rates and the associated low opportunity costs ofthis form of investment. Research also shows that the development of innovative financial instruments, such as the high-yield deposits offered by direct banks, yet available on a daily basis, can also influence the growth of narrow M1. Furthermore, the monetary analysis points to a continued normalisation of the investment behaviour of euro area residents. For a start 9 According to the spoken word, we are seeing acontinued strong increase in MFIs' longer-term liabilities. This development reflects an increased reallocation of assets from assets included in the money supply to longer-term and slightly riskier instruments. On the other hand, we have observed moderate and declining growth in MMF shares in recent months. Whereas these instruments showed annual growth rates of 12% or more between mid-2001 and the end of 2003,their growth fell to only 3.9% in July 2005. The latter are often used to temporarily park liquidity in times of increased uncertainty, when other investments are perceived as too risky. In addition, however, I would like to point outthat the latest data point to a slowdown in the normalization process, which in turn has important implications for price stability. The analysis of M3's counterparts shows that the buoyant development of credit activitycontinues to contribute to M3's strong growth. One of the most striking developments in M3's counterparts is the continued strong growth of MFI loans to the private sector. This development is supported by a broad increase in growth in almost all non-financial sectors. The monetary 10 In addition, the spoken word analysis has been pointing to above-average growth in mortgage loans for some time. The reasons for the briskdemand for mortgage loans are, on the one hand, the historically low real mortgage rates. On the other hand, studies point to the connection to the brisk development of the real estate markets. In some euro area countries,real estate prices have reached their highest level since the early nineties. For this reason, we follow the development of real estate prices with the utmost care. From the current perspective, the rapid expansion of credit appears to be predominantlydemand-driven. For example, the institutions participating in our latest euro area lending survey report a significant increase in net demand for mortgage loans and consumer loans. On the one hand, theresults of our latest survey also point to a greater relaxation of corporate lending guidelines. On the other hand, banks slightly tightened their guidelines for mortgage lending to households. On balance, banks expect a further relaxation of the guidelines for both corporate and household lending in the third quarter of 2005. Overall, the analysis of counterparts calls for particular vigilancein the area of mortgage credit and loans to non-financial corporations. 11 The spoken word is valid As broad money expands rapidly in the second quarter of 2005 and beyond (in July), we see a further increase in excess liquidity. Model-theoretical analyses unanimously point to a positive money gap, both in nominal and real terms. This also applies taking into account portfolio shifts since 2001. It should be noted that the excess liquidity, which is identified as a monetary gap, assumes a "neutral" interest rate levelwhich is well above the present level of interest rates. Nevertheless, in the current situation, there can be no doubt that there is still much more liquidity in the euro area than is necessary to financeinflation-free growth. Another sign of upside risks to price stability over the medium to longer term is that monetary dynamics are mainly driven by developments in the most liquid components of M3. From today's perspective and with regard to the monetary analysis, the assessment of the risks to price stability depends on how the existing excess liquidity is used in the future. On the one hand, the faster the portfolio rebalancing of 2001 and 2002 is reversed, the lower the risks to price stability over the medium to long term. On the other hand, it is of paramount importance, such as the reduction of the number of measures taken in the years 2000 to 2 002 12 The spoken word accumulated money holding proceeds for reasons of caution (I recall here the increased geopolitical and financial uncertainty in the context of the armed conflicts in the Gulf and the accounting scandals). Ifmuch of the accumulated monetary holdings were to be used for transaction purposes in the future, this would pose significant risks to price stability over the medium to long term, especially in times of economic recovery and rising confidence . To sum up, the cross-check on the basis of the monetary analysis suggests that we should remain particularly vigilant with regard to the materialisation of risks to price stability. Against this background, we are also keepinga close eye on longer-term inflation expectations. By firmly anchoring medium-term inflation expectations at levels consistent with price stability, monetary policy makes a significant contribution to a revival of economicgrowth. Against the background of this comprehensive analysis and weighing the risks involved, the Governing Council decided at its most recent meeting to leave the key interest rates unchanged. I therefore hope that I have succeeded in explaining the last monetary policy decision of the Governing Council of the ECB and convincing you of the correctness of this decision. 13

September 2005 Yves Mersch Prsident der Banque centrale du Luxembourg Im Focus der Europischen Zentralbank 1 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, es freut mich sehr, heute einen Beitrag zum Kapitalmarktforum 2005 leisten zu drfen und ich mchte der WGZ-Bank Luxemburg herzlich fr die Einladung danken. Die mir zur Verfgung stehende Zeit mchte ich nutzen, um Ihnen die Herausforderungen der Geldpolitik des Eurosystems aus heutiger Sicht darzulegen und die jngsten EZBRatsentscheidungen zu errtern. Wie Sie sicherlich schon wissen, beschloss der EZB-Rat Anfang September erneut, die Leitzinsen des Eurosystems unverndert zu lassen. Letztere befinden sich seit nunmehr ber zwei Jahren auf ungewhnlich niedrigem Stand. Im August hat wohl kaum eine wirtschaftliche Entwicklung fr soviel Aufregung gesorgt wie die der ansteigenden lpreise, welche auch letzten Monat wieder neue Rekorde verzeichnet haben. Der Wirbelsturm Katrina verwstete Teile der Sdkste der USA und fhrte dazu, da mehrere Raffinerien gegenwrtig und wohl auch in nchster Zukunft nicht betriebsbereit sein werden. Der Anstieg der lpreise bleibt nicht ohne Auswirkungen auf das Wirtschaftswachstum. Das spiegelt sich deshalb auch in den aktuellen Projektionen des Eurosystems wider: die Projektionen fr das reale Wirtschaftswachstum betragen 1,0 bis 1,6 Prozent fr 2005 und 1,3 bis 2,3 Prozent fr 2006. Die Projektionen fr das reale Wirtschaftswachstum hneln damit den Erwartungen anderer Organisationen und sind im Vergleich zum Juni etwas zurck gegangen; dies reflektiert sowohl eine Revidierung des Wachstums im ersten Quartal 2005 sowie gestiegene lpreise. Im zweiten Quartal 2 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort 2005 wuchs das reale Bruttoinlandsprodukt im Euroraum gem der Eurostat Vorausschtzung im Quartalsvergleich um 0,3%, was eine leichte Verringerung um 0,1 Prozentpunkte gegenber dem Vorquartal darstellt und auf das Jahr hochgerechnet ungefhr 1,2% entsprche. Die jngsten Konjunkturindikatoren fr den Euroraum besttigen also ein weiterhin gedmpftes Wachstum. Der lpreisanstieg wirkt sich auch negativ auf Kaufkraft und Verbrauchervertrauen aus. Obwohl der ZEW-Index zur allgemeinen Wirtschaftslage in den letzten Monaten deutlich gestiegen ist, hat sich der Verbrauchervertrauensindikator der Europischen Kommission nicht sprbar verbessert. Den jngsten Daten zufolge erreichte er vielmehr den niedrigsten Stand seit Mai letzten Jahres. Die Einhandelsverkufe sind im zweiten Quartal 2005 im Vergleich zum Vorquartal sehr leicht zurckgegangen, nachdem sie im ersten Quartal noch einen Anstieg um 0,8% aufweisen konnten; mit einem Wachstum von 1,9% ist die Anzahl der PKW-Neuzulassungen dagegen auf dem Vormarsch. Dabei ist zu beachten, da der gemeinsame Beitrag des Einzelhandels und der PKWNeuzulassungen zusammengenommen etwa 45% des privaten Konsums im Eurogebiet ausmachen. Die schwache Inlandsnachfrage im Euroraum steht indessen weiterhin im Kontrast zum anhaltenden Wachstum der weltweiten Nachfrage. Was die Preisentwicklung betrifft, so hat sich der Anstieg der lpreise vor allem auf die Produzentenpreise ausgewirkt: whrend die jhrliche Teuerungsrate des 3 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort Produzentenpreisindex (ausschlielich des Baugewerbes) im Mai 2005 noch 3,5% betrug, betrug die Teuerungsrate im Juni und Juli 2005 je 4,0%. Die Eurostat Vorausschtzung der Jahresteuerungsrate des Harmonisierten Verbraucherpreisindex (HVPI) betrug im August 2,1%, was eine leichte Verringerung zum Vormonat darstellt. Aufgrund der ansteigenden lpreise erwarten wir, da die Jahresteuerungsrate in den nchsten Monaten um diese Werte herum schwanken wird. Den Projektionen des Eurosystems zufolge wird die Jahresteuerungsrate in 2005 zwischen 2,1 und 2,3 Prozent liegen, 2006 zwischen 1,4 und 2,4 Prozent. Die hohen lpreise haben die Inflationserwartungen fr das kommende Jahr ansteigen lassen, weshalb diese Schtzungen betrchtlich hher ausfallen als noch im Juni diesen Jahres (1,8 bis 2,2 Prozent in 2005 und 0,9 bis 2,1 Prozent in 2006). Diesen Entwicklungen zufolge ist es von grter Bedeutung, eventuelle Zweitrundeneffekte bei der Lohn- und Preisbildung zu vermeiden, welche das Hauptrisiko fr die Inflationsaussichten darstellen. Es ist deshalb wichtig, da die Sozialpartner weiterhin ihrer Verantwortung gerecht werden. Folglich wird der EZB-Rat die diesbezglichen Entwicklungen weiterhin mit unablssiger Wachsamkeit (ongoing vigilance) beobachten um sicherzustellen, da die lngerfristigen Inflationserwartungen im Eurogebiet auf einem mit der Preisstabilitt vertrglichen Niveau verankert bleiben. Fest verankerte Inflationserwartungen sind auch fr die Anleihemrkte von besonderer Wichtigkeit. Steigende lpreise verschlechtern die Wachstumsperspektiven und 4 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort erhhen den Inflationsdruck; dies fhrt wiederum dazu, da Marktteilnehmer ihre Zinserwartungen revidieren. Eine eventuelle Abschwchung des Wirtschaftswachstums kann zufolge haben, da die Marktteilnehmer ihre Zinserwartungen nach unten korrigieren, whrend hhere Inflationserwartungen zu einer Aufwrtskorrektur der Zinserwartungen fhren knnen. Nur mit fest verankerten Inflationserwartungen ist es demzufolge mglich, in Zeiten stndig steigender lpreise eine Aufwrtskorrektur der Staatsrenditen zu vermeiden. Infolge des lpreisanstiegs hat sich deshalb die fallende Tendenz der langfristigen Zinsen im Euro-Whrungsgebiet im Verlaufe des Monats August fortgesetzt. Am Monatsende erreichten die Renditen zehnjhriger Staatsanleihen ihren niedrigsten Stand in der Geschichte des Eurosystems; so lagen die langfristigen Zinsen im Eurogebiet bei knapp 3,1%, in den USA hingegen lagen sie bei rund 4,0%. Folglich hat sich auch die Renditedifferenz zwischen zehnjhrigen Staatsanleihen in den Vereinigten Staaten und im Euroraum, welche Ende August unter ihren Monatsdurchschnitt von rund 100 Basispunkten fiel, geweitet. Es wre sicherlich bertrieben, die tendenzielle Abwrtsbewegung der Renditen seit Mitte 2004 voll und ganz den Geldpolitikentscheidungen der Europischen Zentralbank zuzuschreiben. Trotzdem muss betont werden, dass die niedrigen Staatsanleihenrenditen im Zehnjahresbereich zumindest zum Teil auf fest verankerte Inflationserwartungen zurckzufhren sind. Durch eine feste Verankerung der Inflationserwartungen im Rahmen der Preisstabilitt trgt die Geldpolitik der 5 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort Europischen Zentralbank des weiteren zu einer Wiederbelebung des Wirtschaftswachstums bei. Doch nicht nur die langfristigen Staatsanleihenrenditen sind gesunken, denn die Zinsstrukturkurve flachte sich im Verlauf der letzten Wochen weiterhin ab (dies gilt sowohl fr den Eurowhrungsraum als auch fr die USA). So erreichte die Renditedifferenz zwischen zwei- und zehnjhrigen Staatsanleihen im Euroraum Ende letzten Monats 90 Basispunkte, die zwischen fnf- und zehnjhrigen Anleihen 57 Basispunkte. Weil niedrige Staatsanleihenrenditen als Diskontfaktor fr Aktien dienen, tragen sie zu einer positiven Entwicklung der Aktienkurse bei, obschon der Anstieg der lpreise im August auch die Aktienmrkte nicht verschont hat. Besonders im Euroraum hatten die Kurse noch bis Anfang August dank der guten Ertragslage der Unternehmen starke Zuwchse verzeichnet. Der Dow-Jones-Euro-STOXX-Index ist seit Jahresanfang um ber 13% gestiegen, der Standard-&-Poors-500-Index und der Nikkei 225 hingegen legten nur 0,8% bzw. 8,9% zu. Die dynamische lpreisentwicklung hat nicht nur - wie bereits erwhnt - die Renditen langfristiger Staatsanleihen nach unten getrieben und das Verbrauchervertrauen negativ 6 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort beeintrchtigt Marktteilnehmer befrchten auerdem, da der lpreisanstieg weltweit zu einer Korrektur der Wachstumsprognosen fhren knnte. Diese Befrchtungen, die durch das Ausma der Katastrophen in den USA verstrkt wurden, wirkten sich auch auf den Euro-Dollar Wechselkurs aus. Obwohl die Zins- und Renditedifferenzen sich ausgeweitet haben, hat sich die Stimmungslage gegenber der amerikanischen Whrung weiter verschlechtert. Infolgedessen wertete der Dollar seit Juli gegenber dem Euro um rund 3% ab. Somit bte der Dollar einen Teil der im ersten Halbjahr verzeichneten Aufwertung wieder ein. Noch bis Anfang Juli hatte der Euro seine seit Jahresanfang erkennbare Abwrtsbewegung gegenber dem amerikanischen Dollar fortgesetzt. Doch auch Ende August befand sich der Euro nur leicht ber dem Durchschnitt des vergangenen Jahres. Des weiteren sind die rezenten Entwicklungen des Euro-Dollar Wechselkurses auf die Verffentlichungen der letzten Zahlungsbilanzdaten des Eurogebietes zurckzufhren. Die jngsten Daten weisen auf eine sehr starke Steigung der Nettokapitalzuflsse bei den Wertpapieranlagen hin, so da die Marktteilnehmer auch in Zukunft diesen Daten mehr Aufmerksamkeit schenken drften. Zu beachten ist, da der Euro sich im vergangenen Monat gegenber dem Dollar zwar aufgewertet hat, diese Aufwertung jedoch in gewissem Masse durch die Abwertung des Euros gegenber anderen Whrungen ausgeglichen wurde. So blieb der nominale effektive Euro-Wechselkurs im August trotz einiger Kursschwankungen nahezu 7 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort unverndert. In den acht ersten Monaten dieses Jahres hat der nominale effektive EuroWechselkurs sich um 5,7% abgewertet. Auch der reale effektive Euro-Wechselkurs hat sich im Laufe des Jahres deutlich abgewertet, was einer Verbesserung der Wettbewerbsfhigkeit der Exporte des Euro-Whrungsgebietes gleichkommt. Bisher hat mein Beitrag sich auf die wirtschaftliche Lage des Euroraumes beschrnkt. Wie Sie jedoch wissen, unterscheidet die Europische Zentralbank zwischen wirtschaftlicher und monetrer Analyse. Whrend erstere sich auf die Beurteilung der Risiken fr Preisstabilitt auf krzere bis mittlere Sicht begrenzt, bezieht sich letztere auf mittlere bis lngere Sicht. Die monetre Analyse ist deshalb fr die Geldpolitik von essentieller Bedeutung. Seit der zweiten Hlfte des Jahres 2004 beobachten wir einen stetigen Anstieg des Geldmengenwachstums in der Eurozone. Nach einem jhrlichen Wachstum des weitgefassten Geldmengenaggregates M3 von circa 5,4% im zweiten Quartal 2004 belief sich die durchschnittliche Wachstumsrate von M3 im zweiten Quartal 2005 auf 7,2% Prozent. Die jngsten Zahlen fr Juli 2005 deuten auf eine Fortsetzung dieser Entwicklung hin, das Geldmengenwachstum in diesem Monat betrug saisonbereinigt 7,9%. Die Ergebnisse der monetren Analyse verdeutlichen, da das hohe Jahreswachstum von M3 weiterhin in erster Linie von den im Geldmengenaggregat M1 enthaltenen 8 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort liquiden Instrumente getragen wird. Im Juli diesen Jahres erhhte sich die Jahreswachstumsrate des enggefassten Geldmengenaggregats M1 auf 11,1%. Die in M1 enthaltenen liquiden Instrumente tragen damit bereits etwa 4.5 Prozentpunkte zum Wachstum von M3 bei. Jngste Zahlen deuten auf ein weiterhin hohes Wachstum sowohl des Bargeldumlaufs als auch der tglich flligen Einlagen hin. Die rege Bargeldnachfrage ist zum berwiegenden Teil auf den durch die Euro-Bargeldeinfhrung eingeleiteten Anpassungsprozess zurckzufhren. Zum gegenwrtigen Zeitpunkt kann allerdings nicht ausgeschlossen werden, da dieser Prozess letztlich zu einer hheren Bargeldnachfrage konvergiert. Modellgesttzte Analysen deuten ebenso daraufhin, da die anhaltend hohe Nachfrage nach tglich flligen Einlagen zum berwiegenden Teil auf das niedrige Zinsniveau und die damit verbundenen niedrigen Opportunittskosten dieser Anlageform zurckzufhren ist. Untersuchungen zeigen darber hinaus, da auch die Entwicklung innovativer Finanzinstrumente, wie zum Beispiel die von Direktbanken angebotenen hochverzinslichen und dennoch tglich verfgbaren Einlagen, das Wachstum der enggefassten Geldmenge M1 beeinflussen kann. Des weiteren deutet die monetre Analyse auf eine fortwhrende Normalisierung des Anlageverhaltens der Ansssigen des Euro-Whrungsgebiets hin. Zum einen 9 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort beobachten wir einen weiterhin krftigen Anstieg der lngerfristigen Verbindlichkeiten der MFIs. Diese Entwicklung spiegelt eine verstrkte Umschichtung von Vermgen aus in der Geldmenge enthaltenen Vermgenswerten in lngerfristige und leicht risikoreichere Instrumente wider. Zum anderen beobachten wir in den vergangenen Monaten ein moderates und rcklufiges Wachstum bei den Geldmarktfondsanteilen. Wohingegen diese Instrumente in dem Zeitraum von Mitte 2001 bis Ende 2003 Jahreswachstumsraten von 12% und mehr aufwiesen, belief sich deren Wachstum im Juli 2005 auf nur noch 3,9%. Letztere werden in Zeiten erhhter Unsicherheit, wenn andere Anlagen als zu risikobehaftet empfunden werden, gerne dazu verwendet, Liquiditt vorbergehend zu parken. Ergnzend mchte ich allerdings darauf hinweisen, da die jngsten Daten auf eine Verlangsamung des Normalisierungsprozesses hindeuten, was wiederum wichtige Implikationen fr die Preisstabilitt hat. Die Analyse der Gegenposten von M3 zeigt, da die lebhafte Entwicklung bei der Kreditaktivitt weiterhin zum starken Wachstum von M3 beitrgt. Zu den aufflligsten Entwicklungen bei den Gegenposten von M3 zhlt das anhaltend starke Wachstum der Buchkredite der MFIs an den privaten Sektor. Diese Entwicklung wird von einem breiten ansteigenden Wachstum in fast allen nicht-finanziellen Sektoren getragen. Die monetre 10 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort Analyse deutet darber hinaus seit geraumer Zeit auf ein berdurchschnittliches Wachstum bei den Hypothekarkrediten hin. Die Grnde fr die rege Nachfrage nach Hypothekarkrediten liegen zum einen in den historisch niedrigen realen Hypothekenzinsen. Zum anderen weisen Untersuchungen auf den Zusammenhang zu der lebhaften Entwicklung der Immobilienmrkte hin. In einigen Lndern des Euro-Whrungsraums haben Immobilienpreise den hchsten Stand seit Anfang der neunziger Jahre erreicht. Aus diesem Grunde verfolgen wir die Entwicklung bei den Immobilienpreisen mit grter Sorgfalt. Aus gegenwrtiger Sicht erscheint die rasche Ausweitung des Kreditvolumens berwiegend nachfragebedingt. So berichten die an unserer jngsten Umfrage zum Kreditgeschft im Euro-Whrungsraum teilnehmenden Institute von einem signifikanten Anstieg der Nettonachfrage nach Hypothekarkrediten sowie Konsumentenkrediten. Einerseits weisen die Ergebnisse unserer jngsten Umfrage auch auf eine strkere Lockerung der Richtlinien fr die Vergabe von Unternehmenskredite hin. Andererseits verschrften die Banken ihre Richtlinien fr die Vergabe von Hypothekarkrediten an Privathaushalte geringfgig. Fr das dritte Quartal 2005 erwarten Banken per saldo eine weitere Lockerung der Richtlinien fr die Vergabe sowohl von Unternehmenskrediten als auch von Krediten an Privathaushalte. Insgesamt gesehen mahnt die Analyse der Gegenposten besondere Wachsamkeit auf dem Gebiet der Hypothekarkredite und der Kredite an nicht-finanzielle Kapitalgesellschaften an. 11 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort Im Zuge der anhaltenden raschen Ausweitung der weitgefassten Geldmenge im zweiten Quartal 2005 und darber hinaus (im Juli) beobachten wir einen weiteren Anstieg der berschussliquiditt. Modelltheoretische Analysen deuten bereinstimmend auf eine positive Geldlcke hin, sowohl in nominaler als auch in realer Sicht. Das gilt auch unter Bercksichtigung von Portfolioumschichtungen seit 2001. Zwar ist darauf hinzuweisen, da bei der als Geldlcke ermittelten berschussliquiditt von einem neutralen Zinsniveau ausgegangen wird, der deutlich oberhalb des gegenwrtigen Zinsniveaus liegt. Dennoch kann in der aktuellen Situation kein Zweifel daran bestehen, da im Euro-Whrungsraum weiterhin wesentlich mehr Liquiditt vorhanden ist als zur Finanzierung eines inflationsfreien Wachstums erforderlich ist. Als weiteres Zeichen fr Aufwrtsrisiken fr die Preisstabilitt auf mittlere bis lngere Sicht ist zu bewerten, da die monetre Dynamik in erster Linie von der Entwicklung der liquidesten Komponenten der Geldmenge M3 getragen wird. Aus heutiger Sicht und mit Bezug auf die monetre Analyse ist festzustellen: fr die Beurteilung der Risiken fr Preisstabilitt ist mageblich, wie die bestehende berschussliquiditt zuknftig verwendet wird. Zum einen gilt tendenziell: Je schneller die Portfolioumschichtungen der Jahre 2001 und 2002 rckgngig gemacht werden, desto geringer die Risiken fr Preisstabilitt in der mittleren bis langen Frist. Zum anderen ist von grter Bedeutung wie der Abbau der in den Jahren 2000 bis 2002 12 Es gilt das gesprochene Wort akkumulierten Geldhaltung aus Vorsichtsmotiven verluft (ich erinnere hier an die erhhte geopolitische und finanzielle Unsicherheit im Rahmen der kriegerischen Auseinandersetzungen am Golf sowie der Bilanzskandale). Sollte ein Grossteil der akkumulierten Geldhaltung knftig Transaktionszwecken dienen, so wrde dies  besonders in Zeiten einer konjunkturellen Aufhellung und ansteigenden Vertrauens  erhebliche Risiken fr die Preisstabilitt auf mittlere bis lange Sicht beinhalten. Zusammenfassend spricht die Gegenprfung anhand der monetren Analyse dafr, hinsichtlich des Eintretens von Risiken fr die Preisstabilitt weiterhin besonders wachsam zu bleiben. Vor diesem Hintergrund behalten wir auch die lngerfristigen Inflationserwartungen genauestens im Auge. Durch eine feste Verankerung der mittelfristigen Inflationserwartungen auf einem Niveau, das mit Preisstabilitt vereinbar ist, leistet die Geldpolitik einen bedeutsamen Beitrag zu einer Wiederbelebung des Wirtschaftswachstums. Vor dem Hintergrund dieser umfassenden Analyse und unter Abwiegung der bestehenden Risiken hat der EZB-Rat in seiner jngsten Tagung beschlossen, die Leitzinsen unverndert zu belassen. Ich hoffe deshalb, dass es mir gelungen ist, die letzte Geldpolitikentscheidung des EZB-Rates zu erlutern und Sie von der Richtigkeit dieser Entscheidung zu berzeugen. 13

Title: Fiscal Policy in the Monetary Union
text: Pierre Werner Lecture Luxembourg 11 Octobre 2005 FISCAL POLICY : A CHALLENGE FOR THE EUROPEAN MONETARY UNION The subject you chose for this conference is most topical. Monetary policy in the Eurozone is, by definition, common to all countries. But fiscal policies have remained national. Since you cannot normally correct an asymmetric shock or a regional conjonctural divergence by changing the central monetary policy of the European Monetary Union (EMU), you could imagine acting through fiscal policy. That is indeed possible in a federal system like the US : budgetary transfers are automatically directed to depressed areas. But in the case of the European Union- where the European budget only accounts, for some 1% of GDP and is geared to structural funds and agricultural policy-, this tool is not available. In fact, the European Central Bank (ECB) is a Central Bank without a State. Therefore, some form of coordination of national fiscal policies appears indispensable to ensure a smooth functioning of the Monetary Union in order to avoid deep economic divergencies which eventually can be incompatible with the common monetary policy. This is why the Stability and Growth Pack is so essential. With the benefit of the experience of the last seven years, we can attempt to answer the question: "are budgetary rules necessary and do they work?
