Selon Frank Knight, des incertitudes sont des inconnues non connues, par opposition aux inconnues que nous avons identifies et que nous appelons risques. Je ferme cette dgression sur la pense conomique et reviens aux causes de la crise. Parmi les acteurs conomiques, ce sont les banques, je pense avant tout aux banques dinvestissement, qui sont les premires responsables des dfaillances observes. Quatre caractristiques font des banques des acteurs cl dune conomie de march : 4 Premirement, des milliards de paiements requrant des transferts de fonds sont effectus quotidiennement par les banques. Elles grent les systmes de paiements qui sous-tendent les transactions conomiques. En deuxime lieu, les banques et autres intermdiaires financiers empruntent de faibles sommes aux dposants ou aux autres pargnants pour prter des sommes importantes aux investisseurs, sexposant de ce fait  des risques de taux dintrt, de transformation des chances et de contreparties qui les rendent fortement vulnrables  tout changement abrupt des conditions conomiques. Les banques constituent donc un service public particulirement  preneur  de risques. En troisime lieu, ces entits entreprennent des tches ncessaires et essentielles pour le bon fonctionnement de lconomie, en transmettant les ressources des pargnants aux investisseurs et en transfrant le risque de ceux qui ne peuvent lassumer vers ceux qui lacceptent volontiers. Elles sont censes disposer de linformation requise pour exercer cette intermdiation. En quatrime lieu, les banques sont essentielles pour assurer la mise en uvre de la politique montaire. Or, la politique montaire est la politique conomique la plus pertinente pour attnuer limpact des fluctuations et des cycles conomiques et pour maintenir la stabilit des prix. En prenant des risques excessifs, les banques ont failli dans leur responsabilit dintermdiaire qui requiert un trs haut niveau de confiance de la part des dposants et des investisseurs. Toutefois, la premire dfaillance est  mettre sur le compte du gouvernement amricain qui a essay dencourager un trs large accs  la proprit des mnages, en autorisant chaque famille amricaine  obtenir des crdits immobiliers sans prendre en compte son niveau de revenu ou sa capacit  rembourser, crant de ce fait un problme de  slection adverse  par lequel on aboutit  des rsultats inverses de ceux souhaits  cause dasymtries dinformation. 5 Les banques centrales ont elles aussi eu leur part de responsabilit avec des priodes trop longues de taux dintrt artificiellement bas, encourageant un excs de liquidit qui a gonfl les prix dans diffrentes classes dactifs, les marchs boursiers et limmobilier notamment. La Banque centrale europenne est un tout petit saint dans cette glise. Les taux dintrt nayant jamais t aussi bas en Europe quailleurs et je me rappelle vivement que plusieurs chefs dEtat ont tanc la Banque centrale europenne quand elle les a relevs aprs le dernier cycle. Mais les investisseurs sont aussi  blmer pour leur avidit jusque l ingale. Certains investisseurs graient des portefeuilles trs importants dactifs bancaires, de fonds de pension ou dassurance ainsi que des fonds spculatifs et taient donc censs tre dots dune trs grande expertise dans le domaine de linvestissement - une expertise aussi leve que les commissions quils touchaient. Comment est-il possible quautant de ces investisseurs  experts  acceptaient dacheter ces produits structurs avec des notations de double ou triple A sans comprendre leur contenu  cause de lincroyable complexit mathmatique caractrisant leur structure ? La seule raison pour laquelle ils achetaient ces produits tait quils permettaient un rendement suprieur aux produits traditionnels nots AAA- ou AA-, ce qui apparat comme une vritable contradiction en terme de thorie financire. Une autre dfaillance observe  la fois au niveau des marchs et des gouvernements tait lie aux agences de notation de crdit qui valuent les risques de faillite et de remboursement non-ponctuel associs aux actifs mis, achets et vendus dans les marchs. Ces agences de notation taient privilgies dans la mesure o elles ne pouvaient tre poursuivies en justice. Autrement dit, elles ntaient pas responsables, judiciairement ou administrativement (contrairement aux auditeurs), des notes quelles donnaient car elles taient protges par le premier amendement de la Constitution amricaine : leurs employs taient considrs comme de simples  reporters financiers  exerant leur libert dexpression. 6 Un autre point faible de la crise a rsid dans la dfaillance des superviseurs. Dans la plupart des cas, les plus grandes faillites bancaires et les recapitalisations les plus importantes ont t observes dans des pays o la supervision ntait pas assure par la banque centrale mais par le gouvernement. Toutefois, on ne peut attribuer les dfaillances de march aux seuls agents conomiques, que ce soit dans le secteur priv ou public. Les instruments, les stratgies dentreprise et les contrles taient dfaillants. Regardez par exemple le fameux modle  originate and distribute  dans le march des crdits hypothcaires dits  subprimes  ou crdits  risque. Dun ct, la plupart des crdits ntaient pas mis par des banques mais par des agents et des courtiers travaillant  la commission, qui ntaient pas soumis  la supervision et qui navaient besoin que dune licence locale pour travailler dans la vente de produits financiers. Ainsi, ils avaient comme unique objectif de faire signer des contrats de prt  des familles et dempocher la commission sans se soucier si ces familles avaient les moyens ou non de rembourser leur prt. Du ct de la distribution, de nombreuses banques titrisaient les crdits et les revendaient sous forme de produits complexes  des vhicules de conduit, ce qui leur faisait croire quelles saffranchissaient ainsi de tout risque de crdit - une croyance qui sest gnralement avre fausse dans la plupart des cas, les banques ayant souvent accord des lignes de crdit  ces vhicules. En dautres termes, les banques craient un systme comptable parallle, hors bilan, qui transformait des ressources de court terme en des actifs risqus de long terme qui ntaient ni rguls, ni soumis  une quelconque supervision. Les investisseurs qui achetaient ces mmes produits structurs bass sur des crdits  subprime  acceptaient de porter le risque et le financement de ces crdits, car le risque tait sous-valu. Si le Systme fdral de rserve et la Banque centrale europenne avaient forc les banques  rintroduire ces titres dans les bilans (qui nauraient jamais d en tre retirs initialement), les banques auraient d utiliser du capital quelles navaient pas. Cela aurait 7 engendr un asschement du crdit encore plus important que celui que nous avons observ. Le plus significatif de tout cela, cest que sans ces produits complexes et le systme parallle cr, jamais un dysfonctionnement apparu dans le march amricain des crdits subprime titriss naurait affect les banques europennes avec une telle intensit. Un autre problme encore plus significatif repose sur le fait que  de nombreuses banques ont failli dans la gestion de leurs risques. Parfois, comme je lai dj mentionn, elles agissaient sous pression des actionnaires qui souhaitaient un plus grand retour sur investissement ; parfois, le systme de rmunration encourageait une prise de risque excessive. Dautres fois, les directeurs dinstitutions financires pensaient que leur financement  long terme resterait bon march vu le bas niveau des taux dintrt.  Une bonne gestion des risques commence par du bon sens et de la prudence et non par des modles complexes compris par une poigne de physiciens ou de mathmaticiens. Jen arrive aux problmes lis dune part au dveloppement incroyablement rapide des marchs de drivs de gr  gr,  la fois pour les taux dintrt et les marchs des changes et des prts, qui ont atteint des niveaux historiques ; et dautre part aux failles de laccord de Ble II qui permettait un levier accru dans les plus grandes banques, qui savaient quelles seraient recapitalises par les gouvernements en cas de problme de solvabilit et qui taient de sorte incites  prendre plus de risques quune banque ou quun intermdiaire peu  mme dtre sauv. En un mot, la conjonction de ces failles a permis  lindustrie financire toute entire dobtenir des bnfices trop tt, trop facilement et sans gestion de risque approprie. Ce phnomne concidait avec un endettement beaucoup trop important dans le secteur priv et financier. Les tensions sont alles en augmentant et ont culmin dans la crise financire qui a commenc  lt 2007, avec un aggravement svre en septembre 2008 quand la faillite de la banque dinvestissement amricaine Lehman Brothers a mis lconomie globale au 8 bord du gouffre. Aprs le sauvetage du systme dintermdiation financire, un transfert de dettes du priv vers le public qui en 2010 dclenche une crise des signatures souveraines notamment en Europe priphrique. 2. Ractions politiques La crise financire et la dbcle conomique qui sen est suivi ont appel  des ractions politiques sans prcdent des autorits budgtaires et montaires dans le monde entier. Certaines diffrences dans les structures conomiques et financires et dans le fonctionnement institutionnel de la zone euro compar aux Etats-Unis ont conduit  des mesures spcifiques distinctes - visant  atteindre les mmes objectifs, toutefois. Laissez-moi vous expliquer sur quoi reposent ces diffrences structurelles : - Tout dabord, les structures conomiques de la zone euro et des Etats-Unis sont trs diffrentes. Les petites et moyennes entreprises, par exemple, jouent un rle prpondrant dans lconomie europenne. De plus, le secteur public reprsente une grande partie de lconomie europenne et est un actionnaire majeur de certaines banques. Globalement, lconomie de la zone euro est moins flexible que celle des Etats-Unis. Les salaires et les prix sont plus rigides. Laissez-moi vous donner un exemple concret : la frquence  laquelle les prix changent dans la zone euro et aux Etats-Unis. Dans la zone euro, un commerant change ses prix en moyenne au bout de 13 mois. Des tudes montrent que le dlai est de 11 mois pour les producteurs. Aux Etats-Unis, ces dures sont de moins de 7 mois et de lgrement plus de 8 mois, respectivement. Si cette faible flexibilit peut tre un inconvnient en cas de chocs doffre positifs, comme des innovations techniques, en cas de crise, cette relative rigidit europenne a fourni une protection contre des anticipations ngatives excessives qui auraient entran une spirale dflationniste. 9 - En second lieu, il existe galement de profondes diffrences entre la structure des systmes financiers amricain et europen. La composition des sources de financement pour les entreprises non financires, notamment, est frappante. Les petites et moyennes entreprises europennes nont pas daccs direct au march des capitaux mais ont besoin de prts pour financer leurs activits. Dans la zone euro, le financement bancaire reprsente environ 70% du total du financement externe dune entreprise. Aux Etats-Unis,  linverse, les entreprises dpendent bien davantage de sources de financement de march, qui reprsentent 80% du financement externe total. Jaimerais ajouter que le modle de banque universelle constitue le modle dinvestissement prdominant en Europe continentale, contrairement aux Etats-Unis o - bien avant la crise - les banques dinvestissement jouaient le rle le plus important. Dans ses rponses  la crise, la BCE a toujours tenu compte de la structure particulire de lconomie de la zone euro. Par souci defficacit, elle a concentr ses mesures sur le secteur bancaire et sur la provision de liquidit. Aux Etats-Unis,  linverse, la banque centrale sest concentre sur les marchs de capitaux et a achet des actifs directement sur les marchs des capitaux  une stratgie approprie tant donn la dpendance des entreprises amricaines aux marchs des capitaux plutt quaux prts bancaires. Laction de la BCE sur le secteur bancaire sest applique aux trois tapes de la crise en Europe : - Provision abondante de liquidit quand les tensions sur les marchs montaires se sont faites ressentir  lt 2007 ; - Baisse historique des taux dintrt  partir doctobre 2008, quand lconomie a commenc  entrer en rcession. Pour soutenir loctroi de crdit  lconomie relle la BCE a galement recouru  des mesures non conventionnelles visant  soulager les pressions de financement dans le secteur bancaire ; - Interventions dans certains segments de march pour assurer un bon fonctionnement du mcanisme de transmission de la politique montaire,  partir 10 du moment o de svres tensions ont commenc  sobserver dans les marchs de la dette souveraine. Ces mesures fortes et innovantes ont permis de soutenir lintermdiation financire dans la zone euro. En outre, elles ont contribu  maintenir la disponibilit du crdit pour les mnages et les entreprises, tout en tant en ligne avec le mandat primaire de la BCE, le maintien de la stabilit des prix sur le moyen terme. 3. Objectifs  plus long terme 3.1 Un secteur financier sain Au-del de la crise, le secteur financier doit devenir plus rsilient, le fardeau massif de la dette doit tre allg et des endettements excessifs doivent tre enrays dans les secteurs financier, priv et public. A long terme, pour un systme conomique et financier sain et durable, nous devons tendre vers une industrie financire exempte de risque excessif et vers un dsendettement des mnages et des Etats qui connaissent un niveau dendettement excessif. La rglementation et la supervision du secteur financier doivent rduire la probabilit de dfaut dune institution. Un renforcement de la qualit et de la quantit des fonds propres, un ratio minimal de liquidit et une limite au levier, comme demand par le comit de Ble sur la supervision bancaire, visent  amliorer la capacit de lindustrie bancaire  absorber des chocs issus de tensions financires et conomiques, quelle que soit leur source. Enfin, je tiens  prciser que si ces rgles sont a priori efficaces pour limiter les risques de crdit des banques, elles ne peuvent se substituer  un encadrement beaucoup plus troit des superviseurs sur les pratiques de prise de risque des banques. Comme je lai bien indiqu prcdemment, la crise tait davantage lie  une conjonction de pratiques risques et opaques qu une dfaillance du modle traditionnel de la banque universelle. 11 En ce sens, ce nouveau cadre ne peut  lui seul prvenir une nouvelle crise telle que celle observe en 2007-2008. Il doit donc saccompagner dune refonte profonde, en cours dans lUE, dans trois domaines : - Au niveau institutionnel - Au niveau rglementaire ; et - Au niveau des mcanismes de gestion et de rsolution de crise. Comme la stabilit financire est actuellement affecte par le risque souverain, en particulier dans la zone euro, jvoquerai galement les enseignements que nous devons tirer ds  prsent de la crise de la dette souveraine. a) Rforme institutionnelle Au niveau institutionnel, un nouveau cadre pour la supervision micro- et macroprudentielle, le Systme europen de surveillance financire, est entr en vigueur le 1er janvier dernier. Les lgislations europennes qui ont donn naissance  ce nouveau cadre se sont bases sur le rapport dun groupe dexperts de haut niveau prsid par Jacques de Larosire. Cette nouvelle architecture vise  pallier une dfaillance majeure mise  jour par la crise financire : linsuffisante interaction et coordination entre les autorits de supervision nationales, dune part, et la vulnrabilit du systme financier  des risques systmiques interconnects, complexes, sectoriels et transsectoriels, dautre part. Afin de remdier  ces dfaillances, le nouveau systme comprend un Comit europen du Risque systmique (CERS), charg de la surveillance macro-prudentielle, qui runit notamment les gouverneurs des 27 banques centrales de lUnion europenne et est prsid par le Prsident de la BCE. Le CERS a rcemment tenu sa runion inaugurale  Francfort. Il permettra de prvenir ou de mitiger les risques systmiques en assurant la surveillance et lanalyse des risques pesant sur la stabilit financire, en mettant des alertes rapides en cas dintensification de risques systmiques et, le cas chant, en formulant des recommandations quant aux mesures  adopter pour faire face  ces 12 risques. Le nouveau systme comprend galement trois agences europennes de supervision pour les banques, les assurances et les marchs. Ces agences travailleront en rseau et en interaction avec les autorits nationales de supervision existantes afin de veiller  la solidit financire des tablissements financiers eux-mmes et de protger les utilisateurs de services financiers. Elles combineront la supervision nationale des tablissements financiers avec des tches spcifiques au niveau europen qui permettront de renforcer la cohrence dans lapplication des rgles et de favoriser une rglementation harmonise. b) Rforme rglementaire En Europe, la Commission a mis sur la table toute une srie de propositions visant  renforcer la rglementation des services financiers, via notamment une transparence accrue du secteur financier, une meilleure prvention des abus de march, le renforcement de la surveillance, y compris la surveillance des agences de notation et une protection renforce des dposants. Pour certaines rformes comme celle relative au renforcement de la qualit et de la quantit des fonds propres, que jai dj voque, ou celle relative aux normes comptables, la lgislation europenne salignera sur des normes tablies au niveau international. Il est crucial que ces rglementations fassent lobjet dune mise en uvre harmonise au niveau international afin dviter toute distorsion et toute possibilit darbitrage rglementaire qui pourraient gravement affecter la stabilit financire globale. Jajouterais que les forums conomiques ou organes de dcision internationaux qui jouent dsormais un rle accru dans la dfinition de normes applicables au secteur financier gagneraient  souvrir davantage aux centres financiers internationaux, dont la contribution  la nouvelle architecture rglementaire pourrait tre majeure. c) Mcanismes de gestion et de rsolution de crise Parce que malgr le renforcement du cadre institutionnel et juridique de surveillance et de rglementation, les faillites bancaires restent possibles, il est indispensable de mettre en place des mcanismes de gestion et de rsolution de crise, visant  minimiser limpact dune faillite bancaire sur le systme financier et sur le contribuable. Dans lUE, lide dun 13 mcanisme pour la gestion dune crise bancaire transfrontalire est encore au stade de gestation. Consciente que les cots dune rsolution de crise non coordonne augmentent avec le degr dinterconnexion et dintgration des tablissements financiers, la Commission europenne a prsent une communication sur un projet de cadre europen pour la gestion des crises dans le secteur financier. Une solution europenne reste particulirement complexe dans ltat actuel de lintgration europenne, en particulier par rapport aux questions lies au  burden-sharing , au transfert dactifs intra groupe pendant la priode de crise, et  lhtrognit du cadre rgissant linsolvabilit dans lUE. Dans ce contexte, il pourrait tre plus raliste de prparer la voie  une solution intermdiaire : un cadre national de gestion de crise transfrontalire associ  un processus contraignant pour lchange dinformation. Ltablissement de fonds de rsolution nationaux aliments par des contributions verses par les banques permettrait de rduire lala moral et de renforcer la stabilit financire, en limitant la contagion et en vitant la vente dans lurgence des actifs brads, ce qui permettrait de protger largent du contribuable tout en facilitant la rsolution des banques en faillite. Dans ce contexte, la BCL a propos un cadre original de fonds de rsolution exante qui passerait par ltablissement dune structure prive prfinance regroupant la fonction de fonds de garantie des dpts et de fonds de rsolution, qui sont les deux facettes dun mme problme. En fin de semaine, jaurai loccasion de voir le Commissaire Barnier pour lui proposer une date en vue de discuter au sein du Bridge Forum Dialogue de ces questions avec le public luxembourgeois. 3.2 Dfis budgtaires En nous appuyant sur les expriences rcentes, nous devons examiner attentivement le rle de lendettement excessif. Aprs leffondrement de Lehman Brothers en septembre 2008, laccumulation de la dette prive sest arrte, mais le problme de lendettement excessif ntait pas rsolu. Des plans de sauvetage conomiques, limpact des 14 stabilisateurs automatiques et le ncessaire soutien au secteur financier ont entran un puissant levier des budgets publics  des niveaux jamais observs en temps de paix. La dette publique dans la zone euro aura augment de plus de 20 points de pourcentage de 2007  2011. Les chiffres correspondants pour les Etats-Unis et le Japon stablissent entre 35 et 40. Les ratios de dette-PIB approchent les 90% en Europe, 100% aux EtatsUnis et au Royaume-Uni, et 200% au Japon. Le fardeau de la dette doit tre allg et de nouveaux endettements excessifs doivent tre enrays. Cest particulirement crucial en Europe o la politique montaire unique doit tre soutenue par des finances publiques saines. La crise de la dette souveraine qui frappe la zone euro depuis un an a trouv ses racines dans trois manquements qui ont caractris lunion conomique europenne depuis sa cration: le laxisme des politiques budgtaires, linadquation de certaines politiques macroconomiques, et la dficience de la surveillance mutuelle entre les Etats membres. Les rcentes propositions pour rformer la gouvernance conomique europenne et la mise en place du  semestre europen  au 1er janvier pour une surveillance ex-ante des politiques structurelles et budgtaires des Etats membres vont certainement dans la bonne direction et le Conseil de dbut mars devrait dpasser en ambition les propositions de la Commission et du Groupe Van Rompuy de 2010. Il est essentiel de ne pas se limiter au seul redressement des dficits mais dentriner un pacte de rformes structurelles destin  amliorer la comptitivit de la zone euro. En effet des dsquilibres macroconomiques sont  la source des dsquilibres budgtaires. Enfin, le cadre de gestion de crise souveraine labor au cours de lanne 2010, et qui sera renforc en 2013 par la mise en place dun mcanisme permanent, le mcanisme europen de stabilisation, devrait pouvoir tre revu pour accrotre encore la confiance des marchs en la capacit de la zone euro de faire face au risque souverain. En particulier, lactuelle facilit europenne de stabilit financire devrait pouvoir tre comptente pour acheter directement des obligations souveraines. Cela nest nullement incompatible avec la poursuite rigoureuse des efforts dassainissement budgtaires et des rformes 15 structurelles de lensemble des pays de la zone euro, indispensables pour tablir les fondements dune croissance durable  long terme. Conclusion Aprs une stabilisation de lconomie globale depuis le dbut des turbulences financires, nous sommes confronts au dfi de retrouver une stabilit accrue, ce qui passera par diffrentes voies. Etant donn le fardeau massif de la dette dans les pays industrialiss, le potentiel de croissance et les taux de croissance  court terme seront affaiblis par les ncessaires efforts dassainissement budgtaire. Toutefois, une croissance durable et de long terme ne peut tre atteinte quune fois les dsquilibres conomiques fondamentaux traits et les rformes structurelles inities. En Europe, les gouvernements doivent faire preuve de plus dengagement et dambition dans leurs efforts de consolidation budgtaire. Des rgles plus strictes et des seuils minimaux de capital accrus pour lindustrie financire rendront le systme plus fort et plus sain. Mais une rglementation efficace passe aussi par une supervision de terrain base sur la comptence et la proximit. Un juste quilibre devra ainsi tre trouv entre les diffrents niveaux de rglementation et de supervision : national, avec le renforcement des activits de supervision nationale et ltablissement, indispensable, de fonds de rsolution nationaux; europen, avec la ncessaire intensification de la coopration et de la coordination entre superviseurs et de lharmonisation rglementaire, facilite par la mise en place de la nouvelle architecture europenne ; et global, avec une mise en uvre cohrente et raisonnable des normes bancaires internationales vitant les distorsions de march et les dsavantages comparatifs de certains acteurs par rapport  dautres. Je vous remercie. 16

Title: Europe after the crisis  balance between market and state
text: EMBARGO 13.04.2011  14.15 CET Europe after the crisis  balance between market and state Yves Mersch Governor of the Banque centrale du Luxembourg Member of the Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB) Lecture on Economic Policy in the Summer Semester 2011 April 13, 2011, 2:00 pm c.t. Garystrabe 35, 14195 Berlin, Henry-Ford-Bau, Horsaal A - Theword is valid - Dear Dean, Professor Schob, Professor Steiner and Professor Schularick, Dear Sir or Madam, dear students, Thank you very much for the invitation to speak at Freie Universitat Berlin about Europe after thecrisis and the relationship between market and state, freedom and rules. The importance of the exchange between decision-makers from economic, monetary or financial policy as well as academic research has been painfully revealed by the financial and economic crisis. Practitioners need concepts and interdependencies that serve as blueprints for their real actions. And the theorists need practical experience to review the theories and, if necessary, adapt them or even reject them. I will approach the relationship between market and state along the deductive method in the tradition of Aristotle, i.e. draw conclusions from the general to the particular. To this end, I first discuss the core theses of the efficiencymarket hypothesis and the extent to which they have withstood scrutiny by reality. I will then discuss the regulatory and political lessons to be learned from the financial market crisis and in particular from the European sovereign debt crisis . *** The Efficient Market Hypotheses (EMH) essentially goes back to work by Eugene F. Fama and Paul A. Samuelson from the 1960s. According to the efficient market hypothesis, market prices reflect all available information. The hypothesis is based on the idea that prices in a market economy are the result of the decisions of a large number of individual actors. Therefore, they also contain all the information on which these decisions are based. As a consequence, it is impossible for an individual investor to make higher profits than the market, provided that an investor has the same information as the market. In other words, neither institutional nor privateinvestors can beat the market permanently. Or to put it succinctly: The market is always right. Overall, the EMH was a core element of the defining paradigm of Western economics in the 20th century. A major reason for the dominance of the efficient market hypothesis in academic thinking was certainly geopolitical and technological developments. The theory has apparently been confirmed by reality. With the collapse of the Eastern Bloc at the end of the 1980s / beginning of the 1990s, the ideological alternative to Western-style capitalism had finally failed. In addition to the Soviet Union, virtually all sovereign 2 Representatives of actually existing socialism the experiment of the centrally planned economy. With the "Great Moderation", which began in the mid-1980s, the supporters of the free market economy were given further arguments. The "great moderation" conceals the fact that the fluctuations of key macroeconomic indicatorssuch as inflation, employment or national incomes declined significantly. Many market economies grew at acceptable rates, relatively high employment and stable price levels. The idea of the end of the economic cycle made the rounds. In the industrialised world, these developments were symbolically flanked by the election of the Conservative Margaret Thatcher as British Prime Minister in 1979 and Ronald Reagan's rise to US President the following year. Both stood for a strictly supply-oriented course in economic policy with withdrawal of the state, privatization and deregulation of the financial markets. (DE) The progressive spread of modern information and communication technologies has not only boosted productivity for many services. The economists' models and programs were also able to process more and more data with increasing computing power. The impression spread that economics was a science as exact as physics or mathematics. *** With the outbreak of the global financial and economic crisis, the belief in the omnipotence of the free market has been shaken. In the summer of 2007, the first turbulence on the interbank markets began; liquidityon the money market threatened to dry up completely. In September 2008, with the collapse of the Lehman bank, the global financial crisis erupted in full force. As a result, the industrialized world plunged into the deepest recession since the Great Depressionof the late 1920s. In Europe, significant tensions also arose in the government bond markets in May last year. Since then, the market economy as a whole has sometimes fallen into a crisis of legitimacy. Of course, this does not remainwithout consequences for the theoretical foundation. There have always been critical voices within the economists' guild who did not want to sing along to the omnipotence of the market. Even within the mainstream of Western economic sciences,inconsistencies within the theoretical edifice of the EMH have been pointed out. Only a few examples are listed here: How can the existence of entire industries and professions such as rating agencies, data providers, analysts,etc. be explained when the markets work so efficiently? Why do prices temporarily deviate from fundamentally justified prices or how are asset price bubbles and crashes in the financial markets possible? 3 The guild of economists has long takencare of understanding the efficient market hypothesis as an abstract ideal rather than an exact reflection of reality. Among other things, some of the assumptions were relaxed, such as those of the completely rational actors. Instead, naive or irrational players have increasingly been taken into account in order to take account of phenomena such as the widespread use of so-called technical or "chart" analysis, herd behaviour of investors or the influence of interest-based advice and analysis. But the contradictions between theory and reality became ever greater. After all, they accumulated in the financial crisis. Recent research now explicitly tries to explain these contradictions instead of denying them: Empirical studies showthat institutional investors sometimes act strategically or aggressively. For example, hedge funds attack ailing financial institutions through short selling in order to damage or completely get rid of unpopular competition. The prices of the affected institutions cancome under such pressure through extensive short selling that they ultimately disappear from the market and thus from the scene without fundamental justification. It has also been shown that investors may sometimes have undue incentivesto encourage rather than bet against obvious asset-price bubbles such as the dot-com bubble in the late 1990s. It may well be profitable to swim in the stream to the majority of investors over a longer period of time  a behavior that seems understandable, but is in stark contradiction to the theory of efficient markets. (DE) In view of the opacity of complex and structured financial products such as asset-backed securities (ABS), credit default swaps (CDS) and collateralised debt obligations (CDO), the assumptions of perfect information do not stand up to scrutiny by reality. Such products only achieved dubious fame in the course of the financial crisis. They were obviously understood by experts - if at all - only with considerable delay. The major American investor Warren Buffet described them as "financial weapons of mass destruction". *** The financial crisis has thus not only called into question the legitimacy of free financial markets , but that of the market economy per se. In many places, the call for the state is getting louder again. The pendulum swings back. There is a danger that the legitimate desire for improved regulation will result in an excessively tight corset that will ultimately lead to thestrangulation of market dynamics, and that the justified criticism of partial market failure or regulatory failure will lead to the mistaken belief that the state will fix it. Exaggerated faith in the state and asprawling public sector sooner or later lead to bondage or servitude, as the Austrian Friedrich August 4 of Hayek theoretically and practically confirmed the communist movements of the last century. Only inthe social market economy can freedom and prosperity come together. However, those who rely solely on the self-regulation of the market fall short. It is about finding the balance between the market and the state, the appropriate rules that thestate sets so that the freedom of the market can generate the greatest possible but sustainable prosperity and benefits. *** The financial crisis has shown that regulation and supervisors worldwide did not provide sufficient protection. The basicneed for refo rm has become apparent. The aim must be to protect the international financial system from similarly devastating events in the future. Although much research has already been done and numerous academic papershave been published, economics still has a research project for at least two generations ahead of it. Therefore, I will not go into too much detail about the crisis itself at this point, but I will only mention three areas of cause as examples: ( DE) The crisis was triggered by the collapse of the market for junk mortgage loans in the USA, the so-called "subprime mortgages". They were the tip of an iceberg consisting of a lax credit culture, a real estate bubble and excessive consumption on credit. The latent risks in off-balance sheet securitisations and potentised re-securitisations in structured securities of the highest complexity, the aforementioned CDOs, CDS or ABS, were packaged and thus hidden. Through these products, theunderestimated risks were exported from the USA to Europe and other countries. Both private and institutional investors and credit institutions grossly underestimated the risks on the financial markets. Liquidity risks in a globallyinterconnected financial system were also underestimated. The banks' at least formally sophisticated risk measurement procedures and the improved top ratings from rating agencies encouraged overly careless investment behaviour. The seemingly infinite liquidity on the international financial markets and the low yield level of supposedly safe investments also led to the use of ever longer credit levers to drive up the return on equity. In response to the financial crisis, the relevant international bodies are in the process of learning the relevant lessons. The aim is to improve the regulatory framework for 5 Define financial markets to make the global system more robust. In addition, the probability of future crises shouldbe reduced. The central bodies are the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board (FSB). Both are based at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) in Basel. Under the label "Basel III" thefuture substantive rules are defined. They aim to increase the quality, quantity and flexibility of the capital that banks have to hold. This is intended to make institutions more resilient. In addition, liquidity risksand the leverage ratio are taken more into account. The European Union derives binding legal norms for its member states from the globally developed statutes. This approach leads to an absolutely necessary harmonization of national prudential rules in order to ensure a level playing field ininternational competition. Institutionally, a new era in financial supervision began in Europe at the beginning of this year. Three new European Supervisory Authorities (ESAs) and theEuropean Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) have become operational: the European Banking Authority (EBA), the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority (EIOPA) and the European Banking Authority. The Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) will replace the three previous committees of national supervisors as independent authorities. Another lesson from the crisis is that supervisors must not only keep an eye on individual institutions, butalso on the system as a whole. It is important to keep an eye on the forest despite all the trees. In Europe, the ESRB, which is based at the ECB in Frankfurt, plays the role of such a macro-prudential supervisor. Its mission is to 'contribute to the prevention or mitigation of systemic risks to financial stability in the Union'. In addition, the Systemic Risk Board should inform the EU Council about systemic risks and about an impending crisis. It may issue warnings and recommendations in such cases. These are intended to remedy the situation, but also to initiate legislative procedures. *** Much has been achieved in the reorientation of regulation and institutional reform of financial supervision in Europe. I would describe the glass as half full rather than half empty. However, there is still work to be done. (DE) First of all, of course, the new rules must be implemented. The new European Supervisory Authorities also have yet to undergo practical testing. It has, in fact, shifted power from the national to the European supervisory level. 6 given. It is desirable that nationalspecial paths can no longer be taken for protectionist reasons. (DE) The question of how to deal with systemically important financial institutions has still not been conclusively resolved. The idea that a bank is bailed out in the event of a crisis because of its systemic relevance is incompatible with the principles of a market economy. Those who fail in the market must be liable  right up to the ultimate consequence of leaving the market. But if the maxim is "too big to fail", the state and thus the taxpayer become susceptible to blackmail. The apparent false incentives  moral hazard  can ultimately lead to institutions becoming too big to be rescued by the state at all ("too big to rescue"). (DE) As much as the realisation has matured that the reform of regulation and supervision can no longer succeed at national level, it is still unclear how the burden will be distributed if a cross-border institution gets into difficulties and has to berescued. The issue of burden-sharing remains on the agenda. (DE) On the other hand, efforts to call into question financial centres in small countries per se are not effective. It is true that the experience of Iceland and Ireland demonstrates the dangers ofdomestic banks expanding too much abroad. However, this is no reason to place smaller, specialised financial centres under general suspicion. This is evidenced, for example, by the stability of Luxembourg's financial centre. With its focus on asset management and a bankingstructure strongly influenced by foreign subsidiaries, Luxembourg came through the financial crisis relatively unscathed, not least because of effective financial supervision, which also cooperated closely with foreign authorities. This also includes the monitoring of liquidity risks, which is carried out by the central bank. Rather, the innovative strength and customer orientation of specialised financial centres should be strengthened by giving the smaller but systemically important financial centres a voice and a voice in international bodies. ( DE) The regulation of the shadow banking system is still open. Rules must be found for private equity and hedge funds etc. These institutions are not banks in the legal sense. However, they take comparable risks. Should there be strict silo regulation of the formal banking world, there is a danger that the risky transactions will not disappear, but will only migrate to the non-regulated sector. Even within thereformed financial architecture, it is important to maintain a balance. It will be crucial to minimise the likelihood of future financial crises, to make the banking system more resilient, as crises can never be universally ruled out, while ensuring that reformed regulation and supervision ensure adequate and sustainable financing of the real economy. 7 *** However, the need for reform of the institutional framework is not limited to the financial markets. Thefinancial crisis is based on real economic causes. Although the financial crisis and the severe recession that followed originated in the US, it also relentlessly exposed the institutional weaknesses of Economic and Monetary Union. And yet one cannot speak of a crisis of the euro. The single currency is stable and successful. Inflation in the euro area as a whole averaged 1.97% in the first twelve years. The definition of price stability,which underlies the ECB's primary mandate to maintain price stability, tolerates a medium-term headline inflation rate of "below, but close to, 2%". Without exaggeration, this can be described as a "precision landing". The euro is also firmly established as the second most importantreserve currency behind the greenback. Not that the ECB's aim is to encourage the use of the euro as a reserve currency. But the acceptance and confidence enjoyed by this fledgling currency in the world is as clear as the fixed external value of the common currency (which is also not a target variable of European monetary policy). Nevertheless, there is nothing to sugarcoat. Even if there is no currency crisis, it is nevertheless a public finance crisis in some euro area countries. Different paths have led to the national mountains of debt. While some countries provided failed economic stimulus that led, for example, to real estate bubbles,others allowed their domestic banks - not to be confused with a banking sector of foreign subsidiaries - to assume proportions that were no longer proportionate to the size of the country. However, purely fiscal slowdowns, public mismanagementand statistical inadequacies were also observed. Regardless of whether private debt was socialized in the course of the crisis or whether the problem lay in public finances from the outset, the consequence was a drastic increase inpublic debt. Since 2007, debt in the euro area relative to economic output has risen by an average of 20 percentage points. In some countries it increased by 40 percentage points, in a single country even by 70 percentage points. The debt-to-GDP ratio of the euro area as a whole is heading towards 90% of economic output. Just as the global financial crisis began with the collapse of the US investment bank Lehman Brothers, the eurozone's sovereign debt crisis has a single trigger. It erupted when, after the change of government in autumn 2009, Greece announced that its budget deficit would be well above the previously announced 3.7%. As a result, the capital market doubted that Greece would be able to service its debt properly in the future. Other countries with weak public finances were infected by this mistrust. 8 In May 2010, the situation escalated. There was the threat of a disorderly insolvency of Greece. This would have led to serious distortions throughout the euro area. As a result, the EU heads of state and government decided on financial aid for Greece and set up a financial rescue package for the member states of the euro area. This was previously used by Ireland in November 2010. In the meantime, Portugal has also submitted a request to this effect. The discretionary stabilisation measures have saved time. This must be used to improve the economic and financial environment. While Europe's defensive measures and bailouts have been effective during the crisis, the sovereign debt crisis has revealed the need for a fiscal institution that can intervene when acute emergenciesthreaten the monetary union as a whole. This institutional gap was closed by the European Financial Stability Facility (EFSF) and, from 2013, by the European Stability Mechanism (ESM). The permanent crisis mechanism is expected to have an effectivelending capacity of EUR 500 billion. Funds are only granted if moral hazard can be ruled out insofar as a country's own efforts would be slowed down in favour of the prospect of permanent support from financially stronger countries. An emergency ward is important and right in the event of a crisis. However, two unsolved problems become clear in this context: (DE) Firstly, there is a tendency on the part of politicians to show a particularly high level of commitment when it comes to finding new orcheaper sources of funding. The increased rescue package proves this, for example. The more sensible alternative of increasing growth potential with structural reforms and thus reducing dependence on foreign money pots is often neglected. Secondly, there is a mismatch between short-term stabilisation and long-term stability. The European political class has excelled with interventions and concepts when it came to stabilisation in acute emergency situations. Where it was long lacking, however, was the effort to achieve a real culture of stability. One could also say in the rating agencies' rating scaling: stabilization "AAA"  stability "B-". For a real culture of stability in a monetary union in which, despite the common money, there is no common state, clear rules on the financial conduct of the participating sovereign states are required. It was already clear from the design of the euro regime that sound public finances would be a mandatory prerequisite for the stability of thenew currency. However, there was a lack of political will to commit to this stability-oriented budgetary policy in the long term. For some peripheral countries, but also for Germany in the midst of its structural adjustments, thestability and flat yield curve of the euro came in handy. However, the fact that in return a stability-compliant fiscal policy must be provided, especially in boom times, did not meet with enthusiasm everywhere. But that's not all: it was not only in the smaller states of the eurozone periphery that fiscal policy sluggishness spread. The formal fall of the South occurred with 9 the weakening of the Stability and Growth Pact at the instigation of Germany and France in 2005. In this respect, it is to be welcomed that the EU Council and the Commission are pushing ahead with a hardening of the Stability and Growth Pact. Among other things, thisprovides for greater emphasis to be placed on the prevention of fiscal problems and the level of debt. However, the proposals fall well short of what the ECB considers to be a "quantum leap" in the institutional framework. This would require, for example, a real automatism for imposing sanctions in the event of rule violations, which would be removed from political discretion. It is to be hoped that the European Parliament will be able to make improvements at this point. In addition, the corrections must not only begin when fiscal distortions are imminent. These are usually preceded by escalating macroeconomic imbalances. Booming to overheated real estate markets can temporarily conceal the gradualloss of competitiveness and risks to the sustainability of public finances, as well as national banking institutions expanding too quickly across borders. Both phenomena were observed in the eurozone without initially putting undue strain on public finances. It was only when tensions erupted that even seemingly intact national budgets came under considerable pressure. Real prevention therefore starts earlier, specifically in the case ofundesirable developments in economic policy. A monetary union with a single monetary policy and at the same time decentralised fiscal and economic policies needs mechanisms that ensure a balance between the sovereignty of states and their mutual economic dependence. The objective of the 'Euro Plus Pact' is therefore to be welcomed in principle. The heads of state and government of the euro area countries have committed themselves to strengthening the coordination of their national economic policies with the aim of increasing the competitiveness of the euro area as a whole. On the basis of objective criteria such as unit labour costs, experts are asked to assess whether wages develop in line with a country's economic productivity . Each year, concrete national commitments are to be agreed. These are reviewed annually. Although progress has been made on objectives and the regulatory framework, there is cause for concern about the procedure. The most recentinitiatives have increasingly come from individual countries, which then move onto the European policy agenda via the Council. As important as it is that there is agreement, especially between Europe's two largest economies, the internationalgovernance method represents a step backwards in the integration of Europe. The confusion that national initiatives within Europe cause among its citizens has recently been demonstrated by the uncoordinated responses to the uprisings in Libya. On the other hand, the Union method, in which the federal level plays a greater role, symbolises the overcoming of thinking in national categories. Strengthening the Commission and the European Parliament, of course in dialogue with the Council, could also help to: 10 Eurosceptic tendencies, such as have recently been observed sporadically in the party landscape of various countries. The principle had already been clearly discussed during the negotiations on the Maastricht Treaty and later on the Stability and Growth Package. National responsibility in some policy areas, such as those outlined in the "Euro Plus Pact", must not have a negative impact on the pan-European integration of the monetary union. They are subject to Europeansupervisory control, which must also be legitimised by the EU Parliament. As a result, national policies must not destroy European monetary policy. It should therefore be subject to peer pressure at European level. How a country achieves the results compatible with a monetary union remains within national sovereignty. But the result must be right and the disregard must be punished. The financial crisis has shaken the market economy toits foundations as a supporting pillar of a concept of social order. A further crisis of this magnitude would exceed the resilience of public finances and would not be accepted by Western democracies. The ideathat financial markets can regulate themselves has been painfully refuted. But markets are just as inconceivable without fluctuations and tensions as the idea that the state could take over the entrepreneurial tasks in a freedemocratic society and thus replace the market mechanism. What is needed is a robust framework, set by the state, which leaves room for the economy and society to develop within the limits of these rules of the game, withoutcausing harmful excesses. For Europe, and especially for the eurozone, this is a balancing act, because the single currency does not have a single political foundation. Although we have already learned important lessons from the crisis, there is still a lot of work to be done to complete the single currency area through economic union in such a way as to ensure stability and prosperity in Europe. 11
